title.zh: 卷281 列傳六十八 费扬古 马斯喀 佟国纲 阿南达 吉勒塔布 殷化行 潘自龙 额伦特
title.en: Volume 281 Biographies 68: Fei Yanggu, Ma Sika, Tong Guo Gang, A Nan Da, Ji Leitabu, Yin Huaxing, Pan Zilong, E Lun Te
title.raw: 卷281 列傳六十八 费扬古 马斯喀 佟国纲 阿南达 吉勒塔布 殷化行 潘自龙 额伦特

sentences.zh: 列傳六十八

translations.literal: Biographies 68
translations.idiomatic: Biography 68

sentences.zh: 費揚古滿丕碩岱素丹馬斯喀佟國綱邁圖格斯泰

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu, Manpi, Shuodai, Masika, Tong Guogang, Maitugesitai
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu; Manpi; Shuodai; Masika; Tong Guogang; Maitugesitai

sentences.zh: 阿南達子阿喇納吉勒塔布殷化行

translations.literal: A Nanda; his son Ala'na; Jileitabu; Yin Huaxing
translations.idiomatic: A Nanda (and his son Ala'na); Jileitabu; Yin Huaxing

sentences.zh: 潘育龍孫紹週從孫之善額倫特康泰泰弟海

translations.literal: Pan Yulong, Sun Shaozhou; his great-nephew Zhishan; E'lunte; Kang Tai; Kang Tai's younger brother Hai
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yulong and Sun Shaozhou; Zhishan, a descendant in the younger line; E'lunte; Kang Tai; and Kang Tai's younger brother Hai

sentences.zh: 費揚古，棟鄂氏，滿洲正白旗人，內大臣三等伯鄂碩子。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu, of the Dong'e clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner and the son of Esuo, an interior chamberlain and third-rank baron.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu, of the Dong'e clan and a Manchu of the Plain White Banner, was the son of Esuo, an interior chamberlain and third-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 狀貌魁異。

translations.literal: His stature and appearance were outstanding and unusual.
translations.idiomatic: He was striking in stature and bearing.

sentences.zh: 年十四，襲爵。

translations.literal: At the age of fourteen, he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he succeeded to the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，從安親王岳樂率兵徇江西討吳三桂。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, he followed Prince An Yuele in leading troops through Jiangxi to attack Wu Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Kangxi reign (1674), he followed Prince An of the First Rank, Yuele, in campaigning through Jiangxi against Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 三桂將黃乃忠糾眾萬餘自長沙犯袁州，費揚古與副都統沃赫、總兵趙應奎擊敗之，克萬載。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's general Huang Naizhong rallied more than ten thousand men from Changsha to attack Yuanzhou; Fei Yanggu, together with Deputy Commander-in-Chief Wohe and Regional Commander Zhao Yingkui, defeated them and captured Wanzai.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's general Huang Naizhong raised a force of more than ten thousand from Changsha and struck at Yuanzhou. Fei Yanggu, Deputy Commander Wohe, and Regional Commander Zhao Yingkui routed them and took Wanzai.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擊走夏國相於萍鄉，進圍長沙，累戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he drove off Xia Guoxiang at Pingxiang, advanced to besiege Changsha, and won repeated victories in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1676) he repelled Xia Guoxiang at Pingxiang, pressed the siege of Changsha, and won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 十八年，复敗吳國貴於武岡。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he again defeated Wu Guigui at Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1679) he again defeated Wu Guigui at Wugang.

sentences.zh: 師還，擢領侍衛內大臣，列議政大臣。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to senior chamberlain of the guard and enrolled among the deliberative ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was promoted to senior chamberlain of the guard and made a deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹劫掠喀爾喀，遣使諭罷兵，不從，數擾邊境。

translations.literal: Galdan raided the Khalkha; the court sent envoys ordering him to cease hostilities, but he did not comply and repeatedly disturbed the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan raided the Khalkha Mongols. The court sent envoys demanding that he stand down, but he refused and repeatedly harassed the border.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授裕親王福全為撫遠大將軍，率師討之，命費揚古往科爾沁徵兵，參贊軍事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Prince Yu Fuquan was appointed Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief and led an army against him; Fei Yanggu was ordered to levy troops in the Khorchin region and to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1690) Prince Yu of the First Rank, Fuquan, was appointed Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief and marched against Galdan. Fei Yanggu was sent to raise troops among the Khorchin and to serve on his staff.

sentences.zh: 秋，擊敗噶爾丹於烏闌布通。

translations.literal: In autumn he defeated Galdan at Ulan Butung.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Galdan was defeated at Ulan Butung.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，歸化城增戍兵，以費揚古為安北將軍駐焉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the garrison at Guihua City was increased, and Fei Yanggu was made Pacification General of the North and stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year (1693) the garrison at Guihua City was reinforced, and Fei Yanggu was appointed Pacification General of the North and posted there.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，噶爾丹遣使至，請入貢。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year Galdan sent envoys requesting permission to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year (1694) Galdan sent envoys asking to resume tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 費揚古發兵迎護，偵其眾男婦千五百有奇，留之歸化城。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu dispatched troops to receive and escort them, reconnoitered their party of men and women to more than fifteen hundred, and detained them at Guihua City.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu sent troops to meet and escort the party, found more than fifteen hundred men and women, and held them at Guihua City.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，上察噶爾丹意叵測，陽為修好，潛遣入內地窺探，命侍郎滿丕諭責其使，遣之還。

translations.literal: He reported by memorial; the Emperor perceived that Galdan's intentions were unpredictable—that while feigning reconciliation he had secretly sent men into the interior to spy—and ordered Vice Minister Manpi to reprimand the envoys and send them back.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial Fei Yanggu reported what he had found. The Emperor judged Galdan's intentions untrustworthy: he was making a show of peace while secretly probing the interior. The Emperor ordered Vice Minister Manpi to rebuke the envoys and send them home.

sentences.zh: 七月，聞噶爾丹將窺圖拉，詔費揚古偕右衛將軍希福率軍往禦。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, hearing that Galdan intended to threaten Tula, the court ordered Fei Yanggu, together with General of the Right Guard Xifu, to lead troops to defend against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, hearing that Galdan meant to move against Tula, the Emperor ordered Fei Yanggu and General of the Right Guard Xifu to take troops to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 希福請益兵，上責其疑沮，令勿偕往。

translations.literal: Xifu requested additional troops; the Emperor rebuked him for doubt and discouragement and ordered that he not go along.
translations.idiomatic: Xifu asked for reinforcements. The Emperor reproached him for timidity and told him not to accompany the expedition.

sentences.zh: 尋以圖拉無警，慮噶爾丹將趨歸化城，詔費揚古旋師。

translations.literal: Soon, as there was no alarm at Tula but fear that Galdan would turn toward Guihua City, the court ordered Fei Yanggu to withdraw his army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with no threat at Tula but fear that Galdan would strike toward Guihua City instead, the Emperor ordered Fei Yanggu to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，噶爾丹至哈密，費揚古往禦，乃自圖拉河西竄。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year Galdan reached Hami; Fei Yanggu went to oppose him, whereupon Galdan fled west of the Tula River.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year (1695) Galdan reached Hami. Fei Yanggu marched to meet him, and Galdan slipped away west of the Tula River.

sentences.zh: 尋授右衛將軍，仍兼攝歸化城將軍事。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed General of the Right Guard while continuing to hold concurrently the duties of the Guihua garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General of the Right Guard while retaining command at Guihua City.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「聞噶爾丹據巴顏烏闌，距歸化城約二千里，宜集兵運糧，於來年二月進剿。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "I hear that Galdan holds Bayan Ulan, about two thousand li from Guihua City; troops and grain should be assembled for a punitive expedition in the second month of next year."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "I hear that Galdan holds Bayan Ulan, roughly two thousand li from Guihua City. We should gather troops and supplies and launch a punitive campaign in the second month of next year."

sentences.zh: 詔授費揚古撫遠大將軍，以都統伊勒慎，護軍統領宗室費揚固、瓦爾達，副都統碩岱，將軍舒恕參贊軍事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Fei Yanggu Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief, with Commander-in-Chief Yilezhen, Guard Commanders of the Imperial Clan Fayanggu and Wa'erda, Deputy Commander-in-Chief Shuodai, and General Shuxu to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appointed Fei Yanggu Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief, with Commander-in-Chief Yilezhen, imperial clansmen Fayanggu and Wa'erda as guard commanders, Deputy Commander Shuodai, and General Shuxu on his staff.

sentences.zh: 尋召入覲，授以方略。

translations.literal: He was soon summoned to audience and given the strategic plan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon called to court and given his orders in person.

sentences.zh: 三十五年二月，詔親征，三路出師，以黑龍江將軍薩布素出東路，費揚古出西路，振武將軍孫思克、西安將軍博霽自陝西出鎮彝並進，上親督諸軍自獨石口出中路。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fifth year an edict ordered a personal campaign; three routes marched out—the Heilongjiang General Sabusu by the eastern route, Fei Yanggu by the western route, Pacification General Sun Sike and Xi'an General Boji from Shaanxi through Zhenyi in concert, while the Emperor personally directed the armies from Dushikou by the central route.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirty-fifth year (1696) the Emperor took the field in person. Three columns moved out: Heilongjiang General Sabusu on the east, Fei Yanggu on the west, and Pacification General Sun Sike and Xi'an General Boji from Shaanxi through Zhenyi, while the Emperor led the center from Dushikou.

sentences.zh: 上與費揚古期四月會師圖拉。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Fei Yanggu fixed the fourth month for a rendezvous at Tula.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor and Fei Yanggu agreed to join forces at Tula in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 費揚古師自翁金口進次烏闌厄爾幾，再進次察罕河朔，與孫思克師會，而上已循克魯倫河深入。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu's army advanced from Wengjin Pass to Ulan Erji, then again to Chahan Heshuo, where it joined Sun Sike's force, while the Emperor had already pressed deep along the Kerulen River.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu marched from Wengjin Pass to Ulan Erji and on to Chahan Heshuo, where he joined Sun Sike—by which time the Emperor had already driven deep along the Kerulen.

sentences.zh: 五月，費揚古師至圖拉，疏言：「西路有草之地為賊所焚，我軍每迂道秣馬，又遇雨，糧運遲滯，師行七十餘日，人馬疲困，乞上緩軍以待。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month Fei Yanggu's army reached Tula and memorialized: "On the western route the grassy lands have been burned by the enemy; our troops must constantly make detours to feed their horses. Rain has also fallen, and grain transport has lagged. The army has marched more than seventy days; men and horses are exhausted. I beg Your Majesty to slow the advance and wait."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Fei Yanggu reached Tula and reported: "The enemy has burned the pasture on our western line. We must constantly detour to graze our horses. Rain has slowed the grain convoys. We have been on the march more than seventy days, and men and horses are spent. I beg Your Majesty to pause the advance until we can recover."

sentences.zh: 上進次西巴爾台，再進次額爾德尼拖洛海。

translations.literal: The Emperor advanced to Xibaltai and then again to Erdeni Tolohai.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pressed on to Xibaltai and then to Erdeni Tolohai.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹屯克魯倫河，聞上親督師至，升孟納爾山遙望，見御營，大驚，盡棄其廬帳、器械遁去。

translations.literal: Galdan was encamped on the Kerulen; hearing that the Emperor was personally directing the army's arrival, he climbed Mount Mengna'er to look from afar, saw the imperial camp, was greatly alarmed, and abandoned all his tents and equipment in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan was camped on the Kerulen. Learning that the Emperor had come in person, he climbed Mount Mengna'er to look out, saw the imperial camp, and in alarm abandoned his tents and arms and fled.

sentences.zh: 上命馬思喀為平北大將軍，逐噶爾丹，並密諭費揚古要擊，親督大軍躡其後。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Masika Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief of the North to pursue Galdan, secretly instructed Fei Yanggu to intercept him, and personally led the main army in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor named Masika Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief of the North to pursue Galdan, secretly ordered Fei Yanggu to cut him off, and followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 次中拖陵，費揚古偵知噶爾丹走特勒爾濟，遣前鋒統領碩岱、副都統阿南達、阿迪等率兵先往挑戰，且戰且卻，誘至昭莫多。

translations.literal: Halting at Zhongtuoling, Fei Yanggu learned by reconnaissance that Galdan was fleeing toward Tellerji; he sent Vanguard Commander Shuodai, Deputy Commander A Nanda, Adi, and others ahead to offer battle, fighting while withdrawing until they lured the enemy to Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongtuoling, Fei Yanggu learned that Galdan was heading for Tellerji. He sent Vanguard Commander Shuodai, Deputy Commander A Nanda, Adi, and others ahead to skirmish, fighting as they fell back until they drew Galdan to Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 昭莫多者，蒙古語「大林」也，在肯特嶺之南、土臘河之北。

translations.literal: Jao Modo means "great forest" in Mongolian; it lies south of the Khentii range and north of the Tula River.
translations.idiomatic: Jao Modo—"great forest" in Mongolian—lies south of the Khentii Mountains and north of the Tula River.

sentences.zh: 費揚古分兵三隊，東則京城、西安諸軍及察哈爾蒙古兵，屯山上；

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu divided his force into three groups: on the east, the Beijing and Xi'an contingents together with Chahar Mongol troops, stationed on the heights;
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu divided his army into three wings. On the east, the Beijing and Xi'an detachments and Chahar Mongols held the heights;

sentences.zh: 西則右衛、大同諸軍及喀爾喀蒙古兵，沿河列陣；

translations.literal: on the west, the Right Guard and Datong contingents together with Khalkha Mongol troops, drawn up in battle order along the river;
translations.idiomatic: on the west, the Right Guard and Datong troops and Khalkha Mongols formed a line along the river;

sentences.zh: 孫思克率綠旗兵居其中。

translations.literal: Sun Sike led the Green Standard troops in the center.
translations.idiomatic: and Sun Sike with the Green Standard troops held the center.

sentences.zh: 並遵上方略，令官兵皆步戰，俟敵卻，乃上馬衝擊。

translations.literal: All followed the Emperor's plan: officers and soldiers were to fight on foot and mount for the charge only after the enemy gave way.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Emperor's plan, every man fought on foot and mounted for the charge only when the enemy broke.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹眾猶有萬餘人，冒死鏖鬥，自未至酉，戰甚力。

translations.literal: Galdan's followers still numbered more than ten thousand; they fought desperately from the wei hour to the you hour with great ferocity.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan still had more than ten thousand men, and they fought with desperate fury from mid-afternoon until evening.

sentences.zh: 費揚古遙望噶爾丹後陣不動，知為婦女、駝畜所在，麾精騎襲其輜重，敵大亂，乘夜逐北三十餘裡，至特勒爾濟口，斬級三千餘，俘數百人，獲駝馬、牛羊、廬帳、器械無算。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu saw from afar that Galdan's rear ranks did not move and knew that women and camel herds were there; he commanded picked cavalry to strike the baggage train. The enemy fell into great disorder. Pursuing north through the night for more than thirty li to the mouth of Tellerji, they cut off more than three thousand heads, took several hundred prisoners, and captured camels, horses, cattle, sheep, tents, and equipment beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From a distance Fei Yanggu saw Galdan's rear guard standing fast and knew it shielded the women and baggage. He sent elite cavalry against the train. The enemy collapsed. Through the night they chased the fugitives more than thirty li to Tellerji, killing more than three thousand, taking hundreds prisoner, and seizing camels, horses, cattle, sheep, tents, and arms beyond count.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹妻阿奴喀屯素悍，能戰，亦殪於陣。

translations.literal: Galdan's wife Anukhatun was by nature fierce and able to fight; she too was killed in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan's wife Anukhatun was a fierce fighter in her own right and was also killed in the battle.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹引數騎遠竄，費揚古令阿南達詣御營奏捷。

translations.literal: Galdan fled far away with a few horsemen; Fei Yanggu ordered A Nanda to go to the imperial camp and report the victory.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan escaped with only a handful of riders. Fei Yanggu sent A Nanda to the imperial camp with news of the victory.

sentences.zh: 上乃班師，令費揚古駐守科圖。

translations.literal: The Emperor then withdrew the army and ordered Fei Yanggu to garrison Ketu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then withdrew and left Fei Yanggu to hold Ketu.

sentences.zh: 尋命移駐喀爾喀郡王善巴游牧地，诇噶爾丹所往。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to move his station to the pastoral lands of the Khalkha prince Shanba and to scout where Galdan had gone.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to shift his camp to the pastures of the Khalkha prince Shanba and to track Galdan's movements.

sentences.zh: 甫至，噶爾丹潛使台吉丹濟拉率千五百人入掠喀爾喀牲畜、糗糧，遣副都統祖良璧禦卻之，追至翁金河，丹濟拉敗遁。

translations.literal: Hardly had he arrived when Galdan secretly sent the taiji Danjila with fifteen hundred men to raid Khalkha livestock and rations; he dispatched Deputy Commander Zuliangbi to repulse them, pursued them to the Wengjin River, and Danjila was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely arrived when Galdan secretly sent the taiji Danjila with fifteen hundred men to raid Khalkha herds and grain. Fei Yanggu sent Deputy Commander Zuliangbi to drive them off and pursued them to the Wengjin River, where Danjila was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 尋以馬疲，請移軍駐喀喇穆倫。

translations.literal: Soon, because the horses were exhausted, he requested permission to move the army to Karakorum.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with his horses spent, he asked to move his command to Karakorum.

sentences.zh: 會噶爾丹使其宰桑格壘沽英等來請納款，上再幸塞外，駐蹕東斯垓。

translations.literal: At this time Galdan sent his zaisang Geleiguying and others to sue for peace; the Emperor again visited the northern frontier and halted at Dongsige.
translations.idiomatic: About then Galdan sent his zaisang Geleiguying and others to offer submission. The Emperor again traveled beyond the passes and encamped at Dongsige.

sentences.zh: 召費揚古至行在入對，上褒其功，奏曰：「軍中機務，皆遵皇上指授，並未有所效力。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu was summoned to the traveling palace for audience; the Emperor praised his achievements. He replied: "All military affairs in the field followed Your Majesty's instructions; I accomplished nothing on my own.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu was called to the traveling palace. The Emperor praised his service. Fei Yanggu replied: "Every decision in the field followed Your Majesty's orders. I contributed nothing of my own.

sentences.zh: 況西路糧匱馬乏，不能前進。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the western route grain was scarce and horses were worn out; we could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, on the western route we were short of grain and our horses were exhausted; we could not advance.

sentences.zh: 及聞駕至克魯倫，官兵無不奮發，不俟督責，力戰破敵。

translations.literal: When we heard that Your Majesty had reached the Kerulen, officers and soldiers all took heart and, without waiting to be urged, fought fiercely and broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Your Majesty had reached the Kerulen, every officer and soldier took heart and, without waiting to be driven, fought until the enemy broke.

sentences.zh: 奈臣庸劣，皇上窮追困蹙之寇，臣不能生擒以獻，實臣罪也。」

translations.literal: Yet I am mediocre and incompetent: Your Majesty pursued a cornered foe, and I could not take him alive to present—this is truly my crime."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am unworthy. Your Majesty pursued a foe already at bay, and I failed to take him alive. That failure is mine alone."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「噶爾丹窮蹙，朕不忍悉加誅戮，不如撫而活之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Galdan is cornered; I cannot bear to slaughter them all—better to soothe and let them live."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Galdan is at the end of his rope. I cannot bring myself to slaughter them all. It is better to show mercy and let them live."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此天地好生之仁，非臣等所能測也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "This is the benevolence by which Heaven and Earth cherish life—something your servants cannot fathom."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "That is the mercy by which Heaven and Earth cherish life—more than we can measure."

sentences.zh: 賜禦佩櫜鞬、弓矢，命還軍。

translations.literal: He was granted the imperial quiver, bow case, and bow and arrows, and ordered to return with the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gave him the imperial quiver, bow case, and bow and arrows and ordered him back to his command.

sentences.zh: 三十六年春正月，阿南達自肅州奏哈密回人擒獻噶爾丹子塞卜騰巴爾珠爾等，上以其疏錄示費揚古，並賜胙肉、鹿尾、關東魚，諭曰：「時當上元令節，眾蒙古及投誠厄魯特等齊集暢春園，適阿南達疏至，眾皆喜悅。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the thirty-sixth year, A Nanda reported from Suzhou that Hui people of Hami had captured and presented Galdan's son Sebeten Barjur and others; the Emperor had the memorial copied and shown to Fei Yanggu, and also bestowed sacrificial meat, deer tail, and eastern fish, instructing him: "It is the Lantern Festival season; many Mongols and surrendered Eleuths have gathered at the Garden of Exuberant Spring. Just as A Nanda's memorial arrived, all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirty-sixth year (1697), A Nanda reported from Suzhou that Muslims of Hami had captured Galdan's son Sebeten Barjur and others. The Emperor copied the memorial for Fei Yanggu and sent sacrificial meat, deer tail, and fish from the northeast with this message: "It is the Lantern Festival. Mongols and surrendered Eleuths have gathered at the Garden of Exuberant Spring. When A Nanda's report arrived, everyone rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 爾獨居邊塞，不得在朕左右，故以疏示，並問爾無恙，即如與爾相見也。」

translations.literal: You alone dwell on the frontier and cannot be at my side; therefore I show you the memorial and ask after your health—as though we were meeting face to face."
translations.idiomatic: You alone are on the frontier and cannot be at my side. I send you the memorial and ask after your health—as though we were meeting in person."

translations.literal: (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.)

sentences.zh: 二月，上复親征，自榆林出塞，詔費揚古密籌進剿。

translations.literal: In the second month the Emperor again took the field in person, leaving the frontier by Yulin, and ordered Fei Yanggu secretly to plan the advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Emperor again marched in person, leaving the passes by Yulin, and ordered Fei Yanggu to plan the next strike in secret.

sentences.zh: 費揚古以去歲未生擒噶爾丹，請解大將軍任，上不允，令便宜調遣軍馬。

translations.literal: Because he had not taken Galdan alive the previous year, Fei Yanggu asked to be relieved of the post of commissioner-in-chief; the Emperor did not consent and ordered him to deploy troops as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his failure to capture Galdan the year before, Fei Yanggu asked to resign the command. The Emperor refused and told him to move troops as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 費揚古進次薩奇爾巴爾哈孫，丹濟拉使來，言噶爾丹至阿察阿穆塔台飲藥自殺，欲攜其屍及其女鍾齊海率三百戶來歸。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu advanced to Saqier Barhasun; an envoy from Danjila came saying that Galdan had reached Acha Amutai, taken poison, and killed himself, and wished to bring his corpse and his daughter Zhongqihai with three hundred households to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu advanced to Saqier Barhasun. An envoy from Danjila reported that Galdan had reached Acha Amutai, taken poison, and died, and wished to bring his body and his daughter Zhongqihai with three hundred households to submit.

sentences.zh: 費揚古以聞，上乃班師，令費揚古駐察罕諾爾以待。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu reported this; the Emperor then withdrew the army and ordered Fei Yanggu to remain at Chahan Nu'er to await events.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu reported the news. The Emperor withdrew and ordered him to wait at Chahan Nu'er.

sentences.zh: 六月，丹濟拉至哈密。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Danjila reached Hami.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Danjila arrived at Hami.

sentences.zh: 費揚古有疾，詔昭武將軍馬思喀代領其軍。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu fell ill; an edict ordered Pacification General Masika to take command of his army in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu fell ill, and Pacification General Masika was ordered to take over his command.

sentences.zh: 還京師，仍領侍衛內大臣，進一等公，仍以未生擒噶爾丹疏辭，不允，因諭曰：「昔朕欲親征噶爾丹，眾皆諫止，惟費揚古與朕意合，遂統兵西​​進。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he again served as senior chamberlain of the guard, was promoted to first-class duke, and again declined on the ground that he had not taken Galdan alive; this was not accepted, and an instruction said: "Formerly, when I wished to campaign in person against Galdan, all advised me to stop; only Fei Yanggu agreed with my intent, and so led the army westward.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he resumed his post as senior chamberlain of the guard and was promoted to first-class duke. He again declined, citing his failure to capture Galdan alive. The Emperor refused and said: "When I first meant to take the field against Galdan, everyone urged me to stay home. Only Fei Yanggu shared my purpose and led the army west.

sentences.zh: 道路遼遠，兼乏水草，乃全無顧慮，直抵昭莫多，俾奸狡積寇挫衄大敗。

translations.literal: The roads were vast and distant, and fodder and water were lacking; yet without the least hesitation he went straight to Jao Modo and brought the cunning, long-standing foe to a great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The march was long, water and pasture scarce, yet he never hesitated. He reached Jao Modo and broke a cunning foe who had plagued the frontier for years.

sentences.zh: 累年統兵諸將，未有能過之者。」

translations.literal: Among the generals who have commanded armies for many years, none has surpassed him."
translations.idiomatic: In all the years of campaigning, no commander has done more."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「屢出征，知為將甚難。

translations.literal: He also said: "Having campaigned repeatedly, I know how hard it is to be a general.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "After so many campaigns I know how hard command is.

sentences.zh: 費揚古相機調遣，緩急得宜，是以濟事。」

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu deployed according to circumstances, with pace and urgency rightly judged—therefore the affair succeeded."
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu judged when to press and when to wait. That is why the campaign succeeded."

translations.literal: (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.)

sentences.zh: 四十年，從幸索約勒濟，中途疾作，上駐蹕一日，親臨視疾，賜禦帳、蟒緞、鞍馬、帑銀五千，遣大臣護之還京師。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he accompanied the Emperor to Suoyoleji; illness struck him on the way. The Emperor halted for a day, visited him in person to see to his illness, bestowed an imperial tent, python robes, saddle and horse, and five thousand taels of silver from the treasury, and sent ministers to escort him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year (1701) he accompanied the Emperor to Suoyoleji. He fell ill on the road. The Emperor halted for a day, visited him in person, gave him an imperial tent, python robes, a saddle horse, and five thousand taels of silver, and sent ministers to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，賜祭葬，諡襄壯。

translations.literal: He soon died; funeral sacrifices were granted and his posthumous title was Xiangzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after. The court granted funeral rites and gave him the posthumous name Xiangzhuang.

sentences.zh: 以子辰泰襲一等侯、兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: His son Chentai inherited the rank of first-class marquis together with the hereditary office of tosaha.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chentai succeeded to the rank of first-class marquis and to the hereditary tosaha office.

sentences.zh: 費揚古樸直有遠慮。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu was plain and upright and possessed foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu was plainspoken, upright, and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 昭莫多破賊，費揚古令幕府具疏減斬馘之數，備言「師行迷道絕糧，皆臣失算，賴聖主威福，徼幸成功，非意料所及」。

translations.literal: After the victory over the enemy at Jao Modo, Fei Yanggu ordered his staff to prepare a memorial reducing the number of heads cut off, stating in full: "The army lost its way and ran out of grain—all my miscalculation; relying on the sacred ruler's authority and good fortune, we succeeded by chance, beyond what could have been expected."
translations.idiomatic: After Jao Modo he ordered his staff to draft a victory report that lowered the head count and insisted that "the army lost its way and ran out of grain through my errors alone; we succeeded only by the Emperor's fortune, not by any plan of mine."

sentences.zh: 幕府或咎其失體，費揚古曰：「今天子親禦六師，如見策勳，易啟窮兵黷武之漸，非國家福也。」

translations.literal: Some on his staff reproached him for impropriety; Fei Yanggu said: "Today the Son of Heaven personally leads the Six Armies; if he were to see a record of merit, it would easily open the way to incessant warfare—this is not a blessing to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Some on his staff called this improper. Fei Yanggu said: "The Son of Heaven has taken the field in person. A triumphal roll of honors would only encourage endless war. That is no blessing to the realm."

sentences.zh: 及還京師，上嘗命大臣校射，費揚古以臂痛辭。

translations.literal: After returning to the capital, the Emperor once ordered the ministers to compete in archery; Fei Yanggu declined on the ground of pain in his arm.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital the Emperor once ordered the ministers to a shooting match. Fei Yanggu pleaded a sore arm and declined.

sentences.zh: 出語人云：「我嘗為大將事，一矢不中，為外籓笑，損國家威重，故不敢與角耳。」

translations.literal: Going out, he said to someone: "I once served as a great general; if one arrow missed the mark, the outer vassals would laugh and the state's prestige would suffer—therefore I dare not compete."
translations.idiomatic: Outside he explained: "I was once a field commander. One missed shot would make the frontier peoples laugh and diminish the state's prestige. That is why I will not compete."

translations.literal: (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.)

sentences.zh: 滿丕，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Manpi, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Manpi, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 世管佐領，自讚禮郎累遷御史，兼管佐領。

translations.literal: His family held the hereditary company commandership; from master of ceremonies he was promoted step by step to censor while continuing to hold the company command.
translations.idiomatic: His family held a hereditary company command. He rose from master of ceremonies through successive posts to censor while retaining command of the company.

sentences.zh: 以事奪官。

translations.literal: Because of an affair his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his post over a disciplinary matter.

sentences.zh: 從都統郎坦赴尼布楚與俄羅斯使臣議界，還授理籓院郎中。

translations.literal: He followed Commander-in-Chief Langtan to Nerchinsk to negotiate the boundary with Russian envoys; on his return he was appointed director in the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Commander-in-Chief Langtan to Nerchinsk to negotiate the border with Russian envoys and, on his return, was made a director in the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，偕員外郎鄂齊爾賚敕宣示噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, together with Vice Director Eqi'er, he carried an imperial edict to proclaim it to Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1690) he and Vice Director Eqi'er carried an imperial edict to Galdan.

sentences.zh: 時大將軍裕親王福全統師往烏闌布通，上親臨邊指授方略，滿丕以噶爾丹奏書至，因言賊距大軍僅百里，請往擊之。

translations.literal: At that time the commissioner-in-chief Prince Yu Fuquan was leading an army toward Ulan Butung; the Emperor was personally at the frontier directing strategy. When Manpi arrived with Galdan's memorial, he said the enemy was only a hundred li from the main army and requested permission to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Prince Yu Fuquan was then marching on Ulan Butung while the Emperor directed operations from the frontier. When Manpi arrived with Galdan's memorial, he reported that the enemy lay only a hundred li ahead and asked leave to attack.

sentences.zh: 上許之，遂赴烏闌布通督火器營，擊敗噶爾丹，得頭等功牌。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved; he then went to Ulan Butung to direct the firearms brigade, defeated Galdan, and received a first-class merit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed. Manpi went to Ulan Butung to command the firearms brigade, helped defeat Galdan, and received a first-class merit tablet.

sentences.zh: 累擢理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to vice president of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to vice president of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，費揚古進軍圖拉，尚書阿喇尼率蒙古兵為前哨，命滿丕協同經理驛站。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year Fei Yanggu advanced on Tula; Minister Ala'ni led Mongol troops as vanguard, and Manpi was ordered to assist in managing relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year (1694), as Fei Yanggu advanced on Tula, Minister Ala'ni led Mongol vanguard troops and Manpi was ordered to help manage the relay stations.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，命往歸化城協理軍務。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was ordered to Guihua City to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year (1695) he was sent to Guihua City to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征，命將兩藍旗兵赴費揚古軍，自翁金趨圖拉，破賊昭莫多。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, when the Emperor campaigned in person, he was ordered to lead the two Blue Banner troops to Fei Yanggu's army, advance from Wengjin toward Tula, and break the enemy at Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year (1696), during the Emperor's personal campaign, he led the two Blue Banner detachments to Fei Yanggu's army, marched from Wengjin toward Tula, and fought at Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 奉詔還歸化城，察視凱旋官兵行糧，及撫輯降人。

translations.literal: By imperial order he returned to Guihua City to inspect grain for the victorious troops on the march and to settle the surrendered population.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he returned to Guihua City to provision the victorious columns and settle the surrendered peoples.

sentences.zh: 旋仍赴費揚古軍，移駐喀爾喀游牧界外塔拉布拉克，偵防噶爾丹，收降其部人札木素等。

translations.literal: Soon he again joined Fei Yanggu's army, moved his station to Talaburak outside the Khalkha pastoral boundary, reconnoitered against Galdan, and received the surrender of his followers Zhamusu and others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon rejoined Fei Yanggu, moved to Talaburak beyond the Khalkha pastures, watched for Galdan, and accepted the surrender of Zhamusu and others from Galdan's following.

sentences.zh: 未幾，噶爾丹竄死，召還京，列議政大臣，予拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: Before long Galdan died in flight; Manpi was recalled to the capital, enrolled among the deliberative ministers, and granted the hereditary office of tosaha.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Galdan died in flight. Manpi was recalled to the capital, made a deliberative minister, and granted a hereditary tosaha office.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，命往四川勘撫番、蠻，同提督唐希順攻复打箭爐。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was ordered to Sichuan to survey and pacify the Fan and Man tribes; together with Provincial Commander Tang Xishun he recovered Dajianlu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year (1700) he was sent to Sichuan to survey and pacify the Fan and Man peoples and, with Provincial Commander Tang Xishun, recovered Dajianlu.

sentences.zh: 於是雅隴江濱瞻對、喇袞、革布什咱、綽斯甲布諸土目各率所屬戶口投誠。

translations.literal: Thereupon the native chiefs of Zhandui, Laga, Gebushizan, Chuosijiabu, and others along the Yalong River each led their subject households to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The native chiefs along the Yalong—Zhandui, Laga, Gebushizan, Chuosijiabu, and others—then led their people to submit.

sentences.zh: 奏請授五品安撫司，其副為六品土百戶，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that they be granted fifth-rank pacification commissions, with their deputies as sixth-rank native company commanders; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to grant them fifth-rank pacification commissions with sixth-rank native deputies, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 擢正藍旗蒙古都統，以疾乞罷，尋卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Mongol commander-in-chief of the Plain Blue Banner; he begged to retire because of illness and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Mongol commander-in-chief of the Plain Blue Banner, asked to retire on grounds of illness, and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 碩岱，喜塔喇氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Shuodai, of the Xitala clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shuodai, of the Xitala clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 先世居尼雅滿山，有昂郭都哩巴顏者，歸太祖，碩岱其五世孫也。

translations.literal: His ancestors dwelt on Mount Niyaman; one Angguduri Bayan submitted to Taizu, and Shuodai was his fifth-generation descendant.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears lived on Mount Niyaman. Angguduri Bayan submitted to Taizu, and Shuodai was his fifth-generation descendant.

sentences.zh: 初授二等侍衛，兼甲喇額真。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a second-class guardsman and concurrently a jalan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed a second-class guardsman and concurrently a jalan ejen.

sentences.zh: 世祖幸南苑，碩岱與一等伯巴什泰及蒙古侍衛素尼並從。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor visited the Southern Park, Shuodai followed together with the first-class baron Basitai and the Mongol guardsman Suni.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu Emperor visited the Southern Park, Shuodai attended with First-class Baron Basitai and the Mongol guardsman Suni.

sentences.zh: 素尼猝拔刀殺巴什泰，碩岱即舉所執長槍擊素尼，立僕，擒之，置諸法。

translations.literal: Suni suddenly drew his sword and killed Basitai; Shuodai at once raised the long spear he held and struck Suni, who fell; he seized him and had him punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Suni suddenly drew his sword and killed Basitai. Shuodai instantly struck him down with the long spear he carried, seized him, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其勇敢，予世職拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his bravery and granted him the hereditary offices of baitalaburuhan and tosaha.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his courage and granted him hereditary baitalaburuhan and tosaha ranks.

sentences.zh: 授巴牙喇甲喇章京。

translations.literal: He was appointed a bayara jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a bayara jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 從將軍卓布泰南征，渡盤江，擊敗李成蛟。

translations.literal: He followed General Zhuobutai on the southern campaign, crossed the Pan River, and defeated Li Chengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: He followed General Zhuobutai on the southern campaign, crossed the Pan River, and defeated Li Chengjiao.

sentences.zh: 復進攻李定國，度磨盤山遇伏，力戰破之。

translations.literal: Advancing again against Li Dingguo, he crossed Mount Mopan, met an ambush, and broke it by hard fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on against Li Dingguo, he crossed Mount Mopan, ran into an ambush, and fought through it.

sentences.zh: 又從將軍濟席哈討定山東土寇於七。

translations.literal: He again followed General Jixihai to suppress Shandong bandits at Yuqi.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed General Jixihai to put down Shandong bandits at Yuqi.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，擢前鋒統領。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kangxi reign he was promoted to vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign he was promoted to vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，命率兵先諸軍發，駐守荊州。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, he was ordered to lead troops ahead of the other armies and garrison Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, he was ordered to march ahead of the other columns and hold Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋命參贊順承郡王勒爾錦軍務。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to assist in the military affairs of Prince Shuncheng Le'erjin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to Prince Shuncheng Le'erjin's staff.

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷參贊，從將軍穆占等攻長沙。

translations.literal: Before long he was removed from the staff post and followed General Muzhan and others in attacking Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left the staff role and joined General Muzhan in the attack on Changsha.

sentences.zh: 三桂將馬寶、胡國柱等犯永興，碩岱往援失利，棄營入城。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's generals Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, and others attacked Yongxing; Shuodai went to relieve the city but was defeated, abandoned the camp, and entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's generals Ma Bao and Hu Guozhu attacked Yongxing. Shuodai marched to relieve the city, was beaten, abandoned his camp, and withdrew into the walls.

sentences.zh: 穆佔劾之，還京師，罷官，奪世職。

translations.literal: Muzhan impeached him; he returned to the capital, was dismissed from office, and stripped of his hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan impeached him. He returned to the capital, lost his post, and was stripped of his hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，起為正白旗滿洲副都統，從定北將軍瓦岱徵噶爾丹，至克魯倫河，偵賊遠遁，遂還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was recalled as Manchu deputy commander-in-chief of the Plain White Banner, followed Pacification General of the North Wadai against Galdan, reached the Kerulen River, found by reconnaissance that the enemy had fled far away, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1690) he was recalled as Manchu deputy commander of the Plain White Banner and joined Pacification General of the North Wadai against Galdan. At the Kerulen he found the enemy had fled and turned back.

sentences.zh: 尋偕都統噶爾瑪率兵駐大同。

translations.literal: Soon, together with Commander-in-Chief Ga'erma, he led troops to garrison Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Commander-in-Chief Ga'erma in garrisoning Datong.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，大將軍費揚古出師西路，命碩岱署前鋒統領，率大同護軍二百八十人為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, when Grand General Fei Yanggu marched by the western route, Shuodai was ordered to act as vanguard commander and lead two hundred eighty Datong guardsmen as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year (1696), when Grand General Fei Yanggu took the western route, Shuodai was named acting vanguard commander with two hundred eighty Datong guardsmen as the spearhead.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹遁往西路，命費揚古要擊，偵賊至特勒爾濟口，令碩岱率前鋒挑戰，誘至昭莫多，合圍奮擊，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: Galdan fled toward the western route; the court ordered Fei Yanggu to intercept him. Learning that the enemy had reached the mouth of Tellerji, he ordered Shuodai to lead the vanguard to offer battle, lure them to Jao Modo, surround them, strike fiercely, and take heads and captives beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan fled west. Fei Yanggu was ordered to cut him off. When scouts reported the enemy at Tellerji, he sent Shuodai's vanguard to skirmish and draw them to Jao Modo, where the combined force surrounded them and killed or captured beyond count.

sentences.zh: 師還，擢內大臣，复世職，進三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to interior minister, his hereditary rank was restored, and he was advanced to third-class adahahan.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was made an interior minister, his hereditary rank was restored, and he was advanced to third-class adahahan.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-first year (1712).

sentences.zh: 子海綬，於雍正七年以護軍校隨大將軍傅爾丹徵準噶爾，擊賊和通呼爾哈諾爾，陣沒，議卹，予世職拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: His son Haishou, in the seventh year of Yongzheng, followed Grand General Furdan as a guards officer against the Zunghars, fought the enemy at Huitong Hu'erhanuo'er, and was killed in battle; condolence was debated and a hereditary tosaha office was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His son Haishou served as a guards officer under Grand General Furdan in the Zunghar campaign of the seventh Yongzheng year (1729), was killed at Huitong Hu'erhanuo'er, and was granted a hereditary tosaha office in recognition.

sentences.zh: 素丹，富察氏，滿洲正黃旗人，費雅思哈子。

translations.literal: Sudan, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner and the son of Feiyasaha.
translations.idiomatic: Sudan, of the Fuca clan and a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, was the son of Feiyasaha.

sentences.zh: 襲世職，授護軍參領。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary office and was appointed a guards adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the family rank and was appointed a guards adjutant.

sentences.zh: 從裕親王擊噶爾丹，戰烏闌布通，中箭傷。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Yu against Galdan, fought at Ulan Butung, and was wounded by an arrow.
translations.idiomatic: He fought under Prince Yu against Galdan at Ulan Butung and was wounded by an arrow.

sentences.zh: 擢護軍統領，命帥師駐大同。

translations.literal: He was promoted to guards commander and ordered to lead troops garrisoned at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to guards commander and posted at Datong with his troops.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，命素丹發兵與費揚古刻期並進。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi the Emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and ordered Sudan to mobilize troops to advance on a fixed date together with Fei Yanggu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi (1696), during the Emperor's personal campaign against Galdan, Sudan was ordered to march on a fixed schedule with Fei Yanggu.

sentences.zh: 尋召赴行在，統前鋒兵為導。

translations.literal: He was soon summoned to the traveling palace and placed in command of the vanguard as guide.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon called to the traveling palace to lead the vanguard as guide.

sentences.zh: 上次克魯倫河，素丹請俟費揚古軍至夾擊。

translations.literal: When the Emperor advanced to the Kerulen, Sudan requested that they wait for Fei Yanggu's army to arrive and attack from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor reached the Kerulen, Sudan urged waiting for Fei Yanggu so they could strike from both sides.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜內廝馬，改授前鋒統領。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted an imperial stable horse and reassigned as vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he received an imperial horse and was made vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 以疾解任。

translations.literal: Because of illness he resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to resign.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，命大將軍年羹堯徵青海，起素丹參贊軍務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng, when Grand General Nian Gengyao was ordered to campaign in Qinghai, Sudan was recalled to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign, when Grand General Nian Gengyao was sent against Qinghai, Sudan was recalled to his staff.

sentences.zh: 西寧郭隆寺喇嘛助亂，素丹與提督岳鍾琪討平之。

translations.literal: Lamas of Guolong Monastery at Xining aided the rebellion; Sudan, together with Provincial Commander Yue Zhongqi, suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Lamas of Guolong Monastery at Xining aided the rebels. Sudan and Provincial Commander Yue Zhongqi put them down.

sentences.zh: 授正黃旗蒙古都統，署固原提督。

translations.literal: He was appointed Mongol commander-in-chief of the Plain Yellow Banner and acted as provincial commander of Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Mongol commander-in-chief of the Plain Yellow Banner and acting provincial commander of Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 尋改正紅旗滿洲都統，列議政大臣，仍駐守陝西。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Manchu commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner, enrolled among the deliberative ministers, and continued to garrison Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Manchu commander of the Bordered Red Banner, made a deliberative minister, and remained in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 七年，師徵準噶爾，命素丹將西安滿洲兵出涼州，卒於軍，賜祭葬，諡勤僖。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the army campaigned against the Zunghars, he was ordered to lead the Xi'an Manchu troops out from Liangzhou; he died in the army, funeral sacrifices were granted, and his posthumous title was Qinxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1729), during the Zunghar campaign, he led the Xi'an Manchu troops out from Liangzhou, died on campaign, and was granted funeral rites with the posthumous name Qinxi.

sentences.zh: 馬斯喀，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，米思翰長子。

translations.literal: Masika, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner and the eldest son of Misihan.
translations.idiomatic: Masika, of the Fuca clan and a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, was the eldest son of Misihan.

sentences.zh: 初授侍衛兼佐領。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a guardsman and concurrently a company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed a guardsman and company commander.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年，自護軍參領授武備院卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi he was promoted from guards adjutant to director of the Armory.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi (1688) he rose from guards adjutant to director of the Armory.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷鑲黃旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to Manchu deputy commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1689) he became Manchu deputy commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 尋擢內務府總管、領侍衛內大臣，兼管火器營。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, senior chamberlain of the guard, and given charge of the firearms brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became superintendent of the Imperial Household, senior chamberlain of the guard, and head of the firearms brigade.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，馬斯喀率鑲黃旗鳥槍兵以從，先期命與諸大臣議定出征營陣隊伍序次。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, when the Emperor campaigned in person against Galdan, Masika led the musket troops of the Bordered Yellow Banner in attendance; beforehand he had been ordered with the other ministers to fix the order of march and battle array for the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year (1696), on the Emperor's campaign against Galdan, Masika led the Bordered Yellow musketeers. Earlier he had helped the ministers set the order of march and battle array.

sentences.zh: 上駐郭和蘇台，命閱留牧馬群，議分馬群為七，擇水草佳處為牧地。

translations.literal: When the Emperor halted at Guohesutai, he was ordered to inspect the herds left for grazing, and it was decided to divide the herds into seven groups and choose good pasture and water for their grazing grounds.
translations.idiomatic: At Guohesutai the Emperor ordered him to inspect the grazing herds. They divided the herds into seven groups and chose the best pasture for each.

sentences.zh: 上進駐西巴爾台，距克魯倫河已近，而費揚古軍未至圖拉，諭王大臣集行營議。

translations.literal: The Emperor advanced to Xibaltai, already near the Kerulen, while Fei Yanggu's army had not yet reached Tula; princes and ministers were ordered to assemble at the traveling camp for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor advanced to Xibaltai, close to the Kerulen, but Fei Yanggu had not yet reached Tula. The princes and ministers were called to council at the camp.

sentences.zh: 信郡王鄂扎請駐師以待，馬斯喀與內大臣蘇勒達、明珠請進薄敵營，上從之。

translations.literal: Prince Xin Ezha asked to halt the army and wait; Masika, together with Interior Ministers Suleda and Mingzhu, asked to press close to the enemy camp, and the Emperor followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin Ezha urged waiting. Masika, Interior Ministers Suleda and Mingzhu, urged pressing close to the enemy camp. The Emperor agreed with Masika.

sentences.zh: 復進次克魯倫河，噶爾丹望見御營嚴整，遂驚遁。

translations.literal: Advancing again to the Kerulen, Galdan saw the imperial camp in good order and fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the Kerulen, Galdan saw the imperial camp in tight order and fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 上親統師逐之，至拖諾山。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally led the army in pursuit as far as Tuonuo Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led the pursuit himself as far as Tuonuo Mountain.

sentences.zh: 授馬斯喀平北大將軍，率師進至巴顏烏闌。

translations.literal: Masika was appointed Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief of the North and led the army forward to Bayan Ulan.
translations.idiomatic: Masika was named Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief of the North and marched to Bayan Ulan.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹敗於昭莫多，北走，所部丹巴哈什哈等詣馬斯喀軍降。

translations.literal: Galdan was defeated at Jao Modo and fled north; his followers Danbahashha and others came to Masika's army to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Galdan was beaten at Jao Modo and fled north, his followers Danbahashha and others surrendered to Masika.

sentences.zh: 馬斯喀與費揚古師會，收集降人，遣兵★送至張家口外，乃還師。

translations.literal: Masika joined Fei Yanggu's army, gathered the surrendered people, dispatched troops to escort them to the area outside Zhangjiakou, and then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Masika joined Fei Yanggu, gathered the surrendered peoples, sent troops to escort them to the region outside Zhangjiakou, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 列議政大臣。

translations.literal: He was enrolled among the deliberative ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 復從上出塞，率師駐大同。

translations.literal: He again followed the Emperor beyond the passes and led troops garrisoned at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the Emperor beyond the passes and garrisoned Datong with his troops.

sentences.zh: 三十六年春，授昭武將軍，移師駐寧夏，都統巴渾德、齊世，將軍薩布素，都統兼前鋒統領碩鼐，護軍統領嵩祝，總兵王化行並參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-sixth year he was appointed Pacification General, moved his army to garrison Ningxia, and Commander-in-Chief Bahunde, Qishi, General Sabusu, Commander-in-Chief and Vanguard Commander Shuonai, Guards Commander Songzhu, and Regional Commander Wang Huaxing all assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirty-sixth year (1697) he was made Pacification General and moved his headquarters to Ningxia, with Bahunde, Qishi, Sabusu, Shuonai, Songzhu, and Regional Commander Wang Huaxing on his staff.

sentences.zh: 尋命與費揚古會師，馬斯喀以將軍參贊費揚古軍務。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to join forces with Fei Yanggu; Masika, as a general, assisted in Fei Yanggu's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to join Fei Yanggu, serving on his staff as a general.

sentences.zh: 初，伊拉古克三胡圖克圖盜馬歸噶爾丹，及噶爾丹死，复投策妄阿拉布坦。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khutuktu Ilaguksan had stolen horses and returned to Galdan; after Galdan died he again went over to Tsewang Arabtan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khutuktu Ilaguksan had stolen horses and rejoined Galdan. After Galdan's death he went over to Tsewang Arabtan.

sentences.zh: 費揚古令馬斯喀率師追之，次摩該圖，不能及，引師還。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu ordered Masika to lead troops in pursuit; he halted at Mogaitu, could not overtake him, and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu ordered Masika to pursue him. Masika halted at Mogaitu, failed to catch him, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎常綬等諭策妄阿拉布坦，得伊拉古克三胡圖克圖以歸，誅之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Vice Minister Changshou and others to instruct Tsewang Arabtan; Ilaguksan was obtained and returned, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Vice Minister Changshou to Tsewang Arabtan. Ilaguksan was handed over and executed.

sentences.zh: 馬斯喀坐追剿遲緩，當奪官，上命留內務府總管及佐領。

translations.literal: Masika was liable to dismissal for slow pursuit, but the Emperor ordered that he retain the posts of superintendent of the Imperial Household and company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Masika should have lost his rank for the slow pursuit, but the Emperor let him keep his posts as household superintendent and company commander.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，授鑲白旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was appointed Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year (1702) he was made Mongol commander of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，卒，賜白金千，遣內大臣奠茶酒；

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he died; a thousand taels of silver were granted and an interior minister was sent to offer tea and wine at the mourning;
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-third year (1704). The court granted a thousand taels of silver and sent an interior minister with offerings of tea and wine;

sentences.zh: 發引，命皇子往送。

translations.literal: when the funeral procession set out, princes were ordered to escort it.
translations.idiomatic: when the funeral procession set out, princes were ordered to escort it.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬，諡襄貞。

translations.literal: Funeral sacrifices were granted and his posthumous title was Xiangzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral rites were granted and he received the posthumous name Xiangzhen.

sentences.zh: 佟國綱，佟佳氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，佟圖賴子。

translations.literal: Tong Guogang, of the Tonggiya clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner and the son of Tong Tulai.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guogang, of the Tonggiya clan and a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, was the son of Tong Tulai.

sentences.zh: 初隸漢軍，領牛錄額真，授侍衛。

translations.literal: At first he belonged to the Chinese Banner, held a niru ejen post, and was appointed a guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: He began in the Chinese Banner as a niru commander and guardsman.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，襲三等精奇尼哈番，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he inherited a third-class jingqinihafan and was appointed an interior minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi (1662) he inherited a third-class jingqinihafan and became an interior minister.

sentences.zh: 十四年，察哈爾布爾尼為亂，授安北將軍，率師駐宣府。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when the Chahar Burni rebelled, he was appointed Pacification General of the North and led troops to garrison Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1675), when the Chahar Burni rebelled, he was made Pacification General of the North and posted at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 布爾尼亂定，引還。

translations.literal: When Burni's rebellion was settled, he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was crushed, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十六年，推孝康章皇后外家恩，贈佟圖賴一等公，仍以國綱襲。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, in recognition of favor to the empress Xiaokangzhang's maternal kin, Tong Tulai was posthumously made a first-class duke, and Guogang still inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1677), honoring the maternal kin of Empress Xiaokangzhang, Tong Tulai was posthumously made a first-class duke and Guogang succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授鑲黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Chinese Banner commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1681) he became Chinese Banner commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 疏陳世系，請改入滿洲，下部議，許以本支改入滿洲。

translations.literal: He memorialized stating his lineage and requesting transfer into the Manchu rolls; the ministry deliberated and permitted his branch alone to enter the Manchu registers.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on his lineage and asked to be registered as Manchu. The ministry approved the change for his branch alone.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，命與內大臣索額圖等如尼布楚，與俄羅斯使臣費耀多羅等議立約定界。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was ordered, together with Interior Minister Songgotu and others, to go to Nerchinsk and with the Russian envoy Fyodor Alekseyevich and others negotiate and fix a treaty boundary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1689) he joined Interior Minister Songgotu at Nerchinsk to negotiate a boundary treaty with the Russian envoy Fyodor Alekseyevich.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，大將軍裕親王福全率師討噶爾丹，以國綱參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Grand General Prince Yu Fuquan led an army against Galdan, and Guogang assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1690) Grand General Prince Yu Fuquan marched against Galdan with Guogang on his staff.

sentences.zh: 八月己未朔，師次烏闌布通，噶爾丹屯林中，臥駝於前，而兵伏其後。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, day jiwei, the army halted at Ulan Butung; Galdan was encamped in the woods, with camels lying in front and troops ambushed behind.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month the army reached Ulan Butung. Galdan lay in the woods with camels in front and troops ambushed behind.

sentences.zh: 國綱奮勇督兵進擊，中鳥槍，沒於陣。

translations.literal: Guogang urged the troops forward with fierce courage, was struck by a musket ball, and died in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Guogang led a fierce charge, was hit by a musket ball, and fell in the line.

sentences.zh: 喪還，命皇子迎奠。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, princes were ordered to meet it and offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin returned, princes were sent to meet it with libations.

sentences.zh: 將葬，上欲親臨，國綱弟國維及諸大臣力阻，乃命諸皇子及諸大臣皆會，賜祭四壇，諡忠勇。

translations.literal: When the burial was imminent the Emperor wished to attend in person; Guogang's younger brother Guowei and the ministers strongly dissuaded him, whereupon he ordered all princes and ministers to assemble, granted sacrifices at four altars, and gave the posthumous title Zhongyong.
translations.idiomatic: Before the burial the Emperor wished to attend in person. Guogang's brother Guowei and the ministers dissuaded him. He ordered all princes and ministers to attend instead, granted sacrifices at four altars, and gave him the posthumous name Zhongyong.

sentences.zh: 上以翰林院撰進碑文不當意，乃自為製文，有曰：「爾以肺腑之親，心膂之寄，乃義存奮激，甘蹈艱危。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased with the epitaph submitted by the Hanlin Academy and composed the text himself, saying: "You were kin of my innermost flesh and the trust of my heart and backbone; yet you held righteousness above all, took zeal as your duty, and willingly faced hardship and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Dissatisfied with the Hanlin Academy's draft epitaph, the Emperor wrote it himself: "You were kin of my flesh and the trust of my heart; yet you chose duty over safety and willingly faced peril.

sentences.zh: 人盡如斯，寇奚足殄？

translations.literal: If all men were like this, what enemy would not be utterly destroyed?
translations.idiomatic: If every man were like you, what foe could stand?

sentences.zh: 惟忠生勇，爾實兼之！」

translations.literal: Loyalty alone begets courage—you truly possessed both!"
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty breeds courage—and you had both."

sentences.zh: 雍正初，加贈太傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng he was posthumously advanced to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 邁圖，亦佟佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Maitu, also of the Tonggiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Maitu, also of the Tonggiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父烏進，國初自哈達來歸。

translations.literal: His father Wujin submitted from Hada at the founding of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wujin came over from Hada at the dynasty's founding.

sentences.zh: 邁圖初授侍衛，從信郡王多尼下貴州，破明桂王將李成蛟於涼水井，李定國於雙河口、於魯噶。

translations.literal: Maitu was first appointed a guardsman, followed Prince Xin Duoni into Guizhou, defeated the Southern Ming Prince of Gui's general Li Chengjiao at Liangshui Well, and Li Dingguo at Shuanghekou and Yuluga.
translations.idiomatic: Maitu began as a guardsman and followed Prince Xin Duoni into Guizhou, defeating Li Chengjiao at Liangshui Well and Li Dingguo at Shuanghekou and Yuluga.

sentences.zh: 從康親王杰書徇福建，討耿精忠，授行營總兵，戰黃岩，克建陽。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Kang Jieshu in campaigning through Fujian against Geng Jingzhong, was appointed a field camp regional commander, fought at Huangyan, and captured Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Kang Jieshu through Fujian against Geng Jingzhong, was made a field regional commander, fought at Huangyan, and took Jianyang.

sentences.zh: 從將軍拉哈達破鄭錦將何祐於太平山，復興化，拔泉州。

translations.literal: He followed General Lahada in defeating Zheng Jing's general He You at Taiping Mountain, recovering Xinghua, and taking Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With General Lahada he defeated Zheng Jing's general He You at Taiping Mountain, recovered Xinghua, and took Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 從將軍賚塔破錦將劉國軒、吳淑於蜈蚣山，复長泰。

translations.literal: He followed General Laita in defeating Zheng's generals Liu Guoxuan and Wu Shu at Wugong Mountain and recovering Changtai.
translations.idiomatic: With General Laita he defeated Liu Guoxuan and Wu Shu at Wugong Mountain and recovered Changtai.

sentences.zh: 皆有功。

translations.literal: In all these he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In each campaign he distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十五年，授正白旗蒙古副都統兼佐領。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Kangxi he was appointed Mongol deputy commander-in-chief of the Plain White Banner and concurrently a company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Kangxi (1686) he became Mongol deputy commander of the Plain White Banner and company commander.

sentences.zh: 尋署前鋒統領，從征厄魯特，戰烏闌布通，陣沒，諡忠毅，進世職三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: He soon acted as vanguard commander, followed the campaign against the Eleuths, fought at Ulan Butung, was killed in battle, received the posthumous title Zhongyi, and his hereditary rank was advanced to third-class adahahan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting vanguard commander on the Eleuth campaign, fell at Ulan Butung, and was given the posthumous name Zhongyi and advancement to third-class adahahan.

sentences.zh: 格斯泰，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲白旗人，先世居瓦爾喀。

translations.literal: Gestai, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner; his ancestors dwelt in Warka.
translations.idiomatic: Gestai, of the Guwalgiya clan and a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner, came from Warka.

sentences.zh: 父赫勒，歸太祖。

translations.literal: His father Hele submitted to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hele submitted to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 從伐明，攻獻縣，先登。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns against the Ming, attacked Xian County, and was first to scale the wall.
translations.idiomatic: On campaigns against the Ming he was first over the wall at Xian County.

sentences.zh: 入關，西討李自成，破潼關。

translations.literal: After entering the passes he campaigned west against Li Zicheng and broke Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After the entry into China he marched west against Li Zicheng and broke Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 下江南，徇浙江，破明兵嘉興城下。

translations.literal: Descending into Jiangnan, he campaigned through Zhejiang and defeated Ming troops below Jiaxing city.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned south through Zhejiang and routed Ming troops below Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 以牛錄額真授拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: As a niru ejen he was granted the rank of baitalaburuhan.
translations.idiomatic: As a niru commander he was granted the rank of baitalaburuhan.

sentences.zh: 格斯泰初為睿親王護衛，從大將軍伊爾德克舟山；

translations.literal: Gestai was at first a guard of Prince Rui and followed Grand General Yilede in attacking Zhoushan;
translations.idiomatic: Gestai first served as a guard to Prince Rui and followed Grand General Yilede against Zhoushan;

sentences.zh: 從都統瑪奇下雲南，破賊石門坎、黃草壩，克雲南會城：皆有功。

translations.literal: he followed Commander-in-Chief Maqi into Yunnan, defeated the bandits at Shimenkan and Huangcaoba, and captured the Yunnan provincial capital—in all he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: he followed Commander Maqi into Yunnan, defeated the rebels at Shimenkan and Huangcaoba, and took the provincial capital—earning merit in each.

sentences.zh: 累擢前鋒參領兼管佐領。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to vanguard adjutant while continuing to command a company.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vanguard adjutant while retaining command of his company.

sentences.zh: 從國綱戰烏闌布通，國綱戰沒，格斯泰直入賊營，左右衝擊，出而復入者再。

translations.literal: He followed Guogang at Ulan Butung; when Guogang fell in battle, Gestai charged straight into the enemy camp, struck left and right, withdrew, and entered again twice.
translations.idiomatic: At Ulan Butung, when Guogang fell, Gestai charged into the enemy camp, struck again and again, withdrew, and went back in twice.

sentences.zh: 乘勝追賊至河岸，阻於淖，賊麕集，格斯泰力戰，與邁圖等皆歿於陣。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in pursuit to the riverbank, he was blocked by marsh; the enemy massed, Gestai fought hard, and he, Maitu, and others all perished in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to the riverbank he was stopped by marsh. The enemy closed in. Gestai fought on, and he, Maitu, and others all fell in the line.

sentences.zh: 師將發，上賜之馬，格斯泰請自選，得白鼻。

translations.literal: When the army was about to set out, the Emperor granted him a horse; Gestai asked to choose for himself and obtained one with a white muzzle.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army marched out, the Emperor gave him a horse. Gestai asked to choose his own and picked one with a white blaze.

sentences.zh: 或言白鼻古所忌，格斯泰曰：「效命疆場，吾夙原也！

translations.literal: Some said a white muzzle was an ancient taboo. Gestai said: "To give my life on the frontier has long been my wish!
translations.idiomatic: Some said a white blaze was an ill omen of old. Gestai replied, "To die on the frontier has long been my wish!

sentences.zh: 何忌？」

translations.literal: What is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: What is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 師還，裕親王奏：「方戰時，親見一將乘白鼻馬三入敵陣，眾皆識為格斯泰也。」

translations.literal: When the army returned, Prince Yu memorialized: "During the battle I personally saw a general on a white-muzzled horse enter the enemy ranks three times; all recognized him as Gestai."
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) When the army returned, Prince Yu reported that during the fight he had seen a general on a white-blazed horse charge into the enemy lines three times, and everyone knew it was Gestai.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬，視副都統，予世職拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: He was granted funeral honors, treated as a deputy commander-in-chief, and given the hereditary rank of baitalaburuhan.
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) He received funeral honors at deputy-commander rank and a hereditary baitalaburuhan.

sentences.zh: 阿南達，烏彌氏，蒙古正黃旗人。

translations.literal: A Nanda, of the Wumi clan, was a Mongol of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: A Nanda, of the Wumi clan, was a Mongol of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 祖巴賴都爾莽柰，初事察哈爾林丹汗。

translations.literal: His grandfather Baraidur Mangnai at first served Ligdan Khan of the Chahar.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Baraidur Mangnai had first served Ligdan Khan of the Chahar.

sentences.zh: 林丹汗敗走，率所部二百三十餘戶保哈屯河。

translations.literal: When Ligdan Khan was defeated and fled, he led more than two hundred and thirty households of his following to hold the Hatun River.
translations.idiomatic: When Ligdan Khan was beaten and fled, he led more than two hundred thirty households to the Hatun River.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，歸太宗，授一等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: After a year he submitted to Taizong and was appointed a first-class meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he submitted to Taizong and was made a first-class meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 從攻寧遠，敗明兵。

translations.literal: He followed attacks on Ningyuan and defeated Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Ningyuan and defeated Ming troops.

sentences.zh: 復從攻錦州，戰死，贈三等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: He again followed the attack on Jinzhou, was killed in battle, and was posthumously granted third-class angbang janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Jinzhou, fell in battle, and was posthumously made third-class angbang janggin.

sentences.zh: 父哈岱，年十七，從父攻寧遠，敵矢殪父馬且踣，哈岱不遑甲，馳入陣，下馬掖其父超乘，步從擊敵，與俱還。

translations.literal: His father Hadai, at seventeen, followed his father in attacking Ningyuan; enemy arrows killed his father's horse and knocked him down. Hadai had no time to don armor, galloped into the ranks, dismounted to help his father remount, and on foot followed to strike the enemy; both returned together.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hadai was seventeen when he followed his father against Ningyuan. Enemy arrows killed the elder Hadai's horse and threw him down. The son had no time for armor, rode into the line, helped his father back into the saddle, and fought on foot beside him until both returned.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉其勇，厚賚之。

translations.literal: Taizong praised his courage and rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised his courage and gave him rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 父死，襲世職。

translations.literal: When his father died he inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he inherited the family rank.

sentences.zh: 屢從伐明，敗明兵。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns against the Ming and defeated Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly campaigned against the Ming and defeated their forces.

sentences.zh: 入關定江南，徇浙江，擊騰機思，討姜瓖，取舟山，皆在行間。

translations.literal: After entering the passes he pacified Jiangnan, campaigned through Zhejiang, struck Tengjisi, suppressed Jiang Xiang, and took Zhoushan—always in the van.
translations.idiomatic: After the entry into China he helped pacify the south, campaigned through Zhejiang, struck Tengjisi, put down Jiang Xiang, and took Zhoushan—always in the front line.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，授內大臣。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign he was appointed an interior minister.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he became an interior minister.

sentences.zh: 討吳三桂，命與侍衛阿喇尼徵喀喇沁、翁牛特、蘇尼特諸部兵，分駐大同、河南、兗州，備調發。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui was suppressed, he was ordered, together with the guardsman Arani, to levy troops among the Kharchin, Ongniud, and Sunid and post them at Datong, Henan, and Yanzhou as a reserve for dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Wu Sangui he and Guardsman Arani were ordered to raise Kharchin, Ongniud, and Sunid troops and station them at Datong, Henan, and Yanzhou as a reserve.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡勤壯。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Qinzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous name Qinzhuang.

sentences.zh: 阿南達，哈岱次子也，以一等侍衛兼佐領。

translations.literal: A Nanda was Hadai's second son and served as a first-class guardsman while commanding a company.
translations.idiomatic: A Nanda, Hadai's second son, served as a first-class guardsman and company commander.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，鰲拜敗，坐黨附罪斬，聖祖特寬之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi, when Oboi fell, he was sentenced to death for partisan attachment, but the Sacred Ancestor specially spared him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kangxi (1669), when Oboi fell, he was condemned to death for siding with him, but the Kangxi Emperor personally spared him.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，噶爾丹侵掠喀爾喀諸部，命偕喇嘛商南多爾濟齎敕諭罷兵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, when Galdan raided the Khalkha tribes, he was ordered to go with the lama Shangnanduoerji bearing an imperial edict to command a halt to hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1688), when Galdan raided the Khalkha, he was sent with Lama Shangnanduoerji to deliver an imperial order to cease fighting.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹遣使入朝，而侵掠如故。

translations.literal: Galdan sent envoys to court, yet his raiding continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan sent envoys to court but kept raiding as before.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，命往會喀爾喀諸部兵討噶爾丹，以尚書阿喇尼、都統額赫訥等先後率師出塞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was ordered to join Khalkha forces against Galdan; Ministers Arani and Commander-in-Chief Ehene and others led armies beyond the passes in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1690) he was ordered to join Khalkha troops against Galdan while Minister Arani, Commander Ehene, and others led armies beyond the passes in turn.

sentences.zh: 阿南達還奏，言：「噶爾丹為拖多額爾德尼擊敗，偵卒還報，有二人共一騎者，有削木為兵者，狀至窮蹙。

translations.literal: A Nanda returned and memorialized, saying: "Galdan was defeated by the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu. Scouts reported back men sharing one horse, others carving wood for soldiers—their plight was desperate.
translations.idiomatic: A Nanda returned and reported that Galdan had been beaten by the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu. Scouts told of men sharing one horse and others carving wooden weapons—his force was at the end of its rope.

sentences.zh: 請發兵討之。」

translations.literal: I ask that troops be sent to attack him."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that troops be sent to finish him off.

sentences.zh: 上命選察哈爾兵六百，率以赴圖拉，益額赫訥軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered six hundred Chahar troops selected; A Nanda led them to Tula to reinforce Ehene's army.
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) The Emperor chose six hundred Chahar troops; A Nanda led them to Tula to reinforce Ehene.

sentences.zh: 尋阿喇尼請移西路軍會剿，阿南達率兵渡瀚海，會大將軍裕親王福全，敗賊於烏闌布通。

translations.literal: Soon Arani asked that the western-route army be shifted for a joint campaign. A Nanda led troops across the desert, joined Grand General Prince Yu Fuquan, and defeated the rebels at Ulan Butung.
translations.idiomatic: When Arani asked to shift the western column for a joint strike, A Nanda crossed the desert, joined Grand General Prince Yu Fuquan, and defeated the enemy at Ulan Butung.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，命赴寧夏招和碩特部台吉巴圖爾額爾克濟農來降，擢正黃旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was ordered to go to Ningxia to summon the Khoshut taiji Batuer Erkejin to surrender and was promoted to Mongol commander-in-chief of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year (1692) he was sent to Ningxia to win over the Khoshut taiji Batuer Erkejin and was made Mongol commander of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，聞噶爾丹將取糧哈密，授郎坦為昭武將軍，召阿南達還。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, hearing that Galdan meant to seize grain at Hami, the court appointed Langtan Pacification General and recalled A Nanda.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year (1693), learning that Galdan meant to seize grain at Hami, the court made Langtan Pacification General and recalled A Nanda.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，命阿南達如喀爾喀諸部求習塞外途迳者二十人為導​​。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, when the Emperor campaigned in person against Galdan, A Nanda was ordered to seek twenty men among the Khalkha who knew routes beyond the passes to serve as guides.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year (1696), during the Emperor's personal campaign against Galdan, A Nanda was told to find twenty Khalkha men who knew frontier routes as guides.
