sentences.zh: 上次克魯倫河，噶爾丹將走還特勒爾濟，阿南達方從費揚古自圖拉向昭莫多。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached the Kerulen, Galdan was about to flee back toward Tellerji. A Nanda was then coming from Fei Yanggu from Tula toward Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor reached the Kerulen, Galdan was turning back toward Tellerji. A Nanda was marching from Fei Yanggu at Tula toward Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 費揚古令阿南達等先擊噶爾丹，偽敗以致敵，至昭莫多，縱擊敗敵，事具費揚古傳。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu ordered A Nanda and others to strike Galdan first, feign defeat to draw the enemy on, and at Jao Modo release a full attack and rout them—the affair is set forth in Fei Yanggu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu had A Nanda strike first, pretend defeat to lure Galdan on, then at Jao Modo crush him—the full account is in Fei Yanggu's biography.

sentences.zh: 阿南達赴行在奏捷，上召詢戰狀，對曰：「噶爾丹聞上親征，惶駭竄走。

translations.literal: A Nanda went to the imperial camp to report victory. The Emperor summoned him to ask about the battle. He answered: "Galdan, hearing that Your Majesty was campaigning in person, fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: A Nanda reported victory at the imperial camp. Asked about the fight, he said Galdan had fled in panic when he learned the Emperor was in the field.

sentences.zh: 不虞我兵絕其歸路，突然交戰，擒斬過半，死傷枕藉。

translations.literal: He did not expect our troops to cut off his retreat. We engaged suddenly; more than half were captured or killed, and the dead and wounded lay piled together.
translations.idiomatic: He did not expect our troops to block his retreat. We struck suddenly; more than half were killed or captured, and the ground was heaped with dead and wounded.

sentences.zh: 屬下人多怨懟，降者甚眾，噶爾丹深以為悔。

translations.literal: Many of his followers were resentful; very many surrendered. Galdan deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: His followers were bitter; many surrendered. Galdan was filled with remorse.

sentences.zh: 費揚古慮涉矜張，疏報捷，特約略言之。」

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu, fearing exaggeration, reported victory in a memorial and spoke only in general terms."
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu, fearing boastfulness, reported victory in restrained terms.

sentences.zh: 上乃班師，命阿南達駐守肅州。

translations.literal: The Emperor then withdrew the army and ordered A Nanda to garrison Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) The Emperor then withdrew and ordered A Nanda to hold Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋移軍邊境，诇噶爾丹踪跡。

translations.literal: He soon moved troops to the border to scout Galdan's tracks.
translations.idiomatic: He soon shifted troops to the frontier to track Galdan.

sentences.zh: 阿南達遣兵分駐昆都倫、額濟內諸處。

translations.literal: A Nanda sent troops to post separately at Qundulun, Ejine, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: A Nanda posted detachments at Qundulun, Ejine, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 復與提督李林隆移砲赴布隆吉爾，度要隘留軍策應，乃還肅州。

translations.literal: He again moved artillery with Provincial Commander Li Linlong to Bulongji'er, judged key passes, left troops to support one another, and then returned to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Provincial Commander Li Linlong he moved guns to Bulongji'er, secured the passes with supporting garrisons, and returned to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 上以其章示議政諸臣，獎阿南達防邊能稱職也。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed his memorial to the deliberative ministers and praised A Nanda for performing frontier defense well.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor showed his memorial to the deliberative ministers and praised A Nanda for competent frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹自昭莫多敗後，部眾多離散。

translations.literal: After Galdan's defeat at Jao Modo, many of his followers scattered.
translations.idiomatic: After Galdan's defeat at Jao Modo, many of his followers deserted.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹多爾濟者，其妻弟也，陰持兩端。

translations.literal: Galdandorji was his wife's younger brother and secretly kept to both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Galdandorji, his brother-in-law, secretly wavered between both sides.

sentences.zh: 阿南達至布隆吉爾，獲其邏卒，縱歸招之降，遂遣使通款。

translations.literal: When A Nanda reached Bulongji'er he captured Galdandorji's scouts, released them to summon his surrender, and Galdandorji then sent envoys to open negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: At Bulongji'er A Nanda took Galdandorji's scouts, sent them back to offer surrender, and Galdandorji opened talks.

sentences.zh: 阿南達因其使檄哈密回部：「噶爾丹且至，當擒獻。」

translations.literal: A Nanda used his envoy to proclaim to the Hami Muslims: "Galdan is coming; you must seize and hand him over."
translations.idiomatic: A Nanda used the envoy to warn the Hami Muslims that Galdan was coming and they must seize and deliver him.

sentences.zh: 即傳語噶爾丹多爾濟：「噶爾丹至哈密，哈密且擒獻，當為哈密助。」

translations.literal: He then sent word to Galdandorji: "When Galdan reaches Hami, Hami will seize and hand him over; we shall aid Hami."
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) He told Galdandorji that when Galdan reached Hami the city would seize him and the court would help Hami do it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，噶爾丹遣族子顧孟多爾濟等與達賴喇嘛、青海諸台吉通聲聞。

translations.literal: Before long, Galdan sent his clansman Gumdorji and others to communicate with the Dalai Lama and the Qinghai taiji.
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) Soon Galdan sent his kinsman Gumdorji and others to contact the Dalai Lama and the Qinghai taiji.

sentences.zh: 阿南達復至布隆吉爾偵知之，率兵追及於素爾河，擒其使人，以其書十四函馳奏。

translations.literal: A Nanda again came to Bulongji'er, learned this by reconnaissance, led troops in pursuit to the Su'er River, captured his envoys, and hurried a memorial with fourteen of their letters.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Bulongji'er he learned this by scouts, pursued to the Su'er River, seized the envoys, and rushed a memorial with fourteen of their letters.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，哈密回部擒噶爾丹子色卜騰巴爾珠爾及其從者徽特和碩齊等，送阿南達。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year the Hami Muslims captured Galdan's son Sebetenbaljur and his followers Weiteheshuoqi and others and sent them to A Nanda.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year (1697) Hami Muslims seized Galdan's son Sebetenbaljur and followers including Weiteheshuoqi and sent them to A Nanda.

sentences.zh: 繼又獲厄魯特土克齊哈什哈。

translations.literal: They then also captured the Eleuth Tukqi Hasha.
translations.idiomatic: They soon also captured the Eleuth Tukqi Hasha.

sentences.zh: 土克齊哈什哈實戕我使臣馬迪，至是始就擒。

translations.literal: Tukqi Hasha had in fact killed our envoy Madi; only now was he taken.
translations.idiomatic: Tukqi Hasha had killed the envoy Madi; only now was he captured.

sentences.zh: 先後檻送京師。

translations.literal: In succession they were sent to the capital in cages.
translations.idiomatic: Both were sent to the capital in cages.

sentences.zh: 尋复疏言厄魯特晉巴徹爾貝來降，詢知噶爾丹窮促狀。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized again that the Eleuth Jinbacheerbe had come to surrender and reported Galdan's desperate condition.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that the Eleuth Jinbacheerbe had surrendered and described Galdan's desperate state.

sentences.zh: 是歲上复親征，命與林隆率甘州兵二千出布隆吉爾。

translations.literal: That year the Emperor again campaigned in person and ordered him, with Linlong, to lead two thousand Gansu troops out from Bulongji'er.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Emperor campaigned again and ordered him and Linlong to lead two thousand Gansu troops from Bulongji'er.

sentences.zh: 次塔爾河，聞噶爾丹已死，所部台吉丹濟拉將竄巴里坤依噶爾丹從子策妄阿喇布坦，因往追之，未及，上命還駐布隆吉爾。

translations.literal: Halting at the Ta'er River, they heard Galdan was dead. The taiji Danjila was about to flee to Barkul and rely on Galdan's nephew Tsewang Arabtan, so they went in pursuit but did not overtake him; the Emperor ordered them back to garrison Bulongji'er.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ta'er River they learned Galdan was dead. The taiji Danjila was fleeing toward Barkul to join Galdan's nephew Tsewang Arabtan; they pursued but missed him, and the Emperor ordered them back to Bulongji'er.

sentences.zh: 丹濟拉詣哈密乞降，阿南達護使謁上行在。

translations.literal: Danjila came to Hami to beg surrender; A Nanda escorted his envoy to audience at the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Danjila surrendered at Hami; A Nanda escorted his envoy to the Emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 敘昭莫多功，予拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: For merit at Jao Modo he was granted the hereditary rank of tosaha.
translations.idiomatic: For Jao Modo he received a hereditary tosaha rank.

sentences.zh: 尋奉命率兵駐西寧。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to lead troops to garrison Xining.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to garrison Xining with his troops.

sentences.zh: 四十年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he died and was granted funeral honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year (1701) he died and received funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，追諡恪敏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng he was posthumously given the title Kemin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongzheng (1724) he was posthumously named Kemin.

sentences.zh: 阿喇納，阿南達長子。

translations.literal: Ala'na was A Nanda's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Ala'na was A Nanda's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 少襲其祖哈岱世職，授三等侍衛，累進散秩大臣。

translations.literal: In youth he inherited his grandfather Hadai's hereditary office, was appointed a third-class guardsman, and was promoted step by step to honorary grand minister.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he inherited his grandfather Hadai's rank, became a third-class guardsman, and rose to honorary grand minister.

sentences.zh: 策妄阿喇布坦繼噶爾丹為寇，侵哈密。

translations.literal: Tsewang Arabtan succeeded Galdan as a raider and invaded Hami.
translations.idiomatic: Tsewang Arabtan succeeded Galdan as a border foe and invaded Hami.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十四年，上命尚書富寧安視師，屯巴爾庫爾。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi the Emperor ordered Minister Funinggan to take command and encamp at Barkul.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi (1715) the Emperor ordered Minister Funinggan to take the field and encamp at Barkul.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，授阿喇納參贊大臣，選八旗察哈爾勁卒及嘗從阿南達出塞者，得四百人，率之以行。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year Ala'na was appointed staff minister. He chose stalwart Chahar soldiers from the Eight Banners and men who had once followed A Nanda beyond the passes, obtained four hundred, and led them on the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year (1716) Ala'na became staff minister, picked four hundred elite Chahar troops and veterans of A Nanda's frontier campaigns, and marched with them.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，授富寧安靖逆大將軍，令阿喇納將一千三百人，自烏闌烏蘇深入烏魯木齊。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year Funinggan was made Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief for the suppression of rebels and ordered Ala'na to lead thirteen hundred men from Ulan Usu deep into Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year (1717) Funinggan became Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief; Ala'na led thirteen hundred men from Ulan Usu into Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 至通俄巴錫搜山，俘一百數十人，收駝馬牛羊，躪其稼乃還。

translations.literal: At Tong'e Baxisou Mountain they captured more than one hundred and several tens of men, took camels, horses, and cattle, trampled their crops, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong'e Baxisou Mountain they took more than a hundred prisoners, seized herds, ruined the crops, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，師入西藏，富寧安復令率四千人自吐魯番出邊，至齊克塔木，破賊敵壘。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, when the army entered Tibet, Funinggan again ordered him to lead four thousand men from Turfan beyond the border to Qiketamu and break the enemy stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year (1720), during the Tibet campaign, Funinggan sent him with four thousand men from Turfan to Qiketamu to storm an enemy fort.

sentences.zh: 進至皮禪，回民三百餘以城降，師遂會富寧安於烏闌烏蘇，引還。

translations.literal: Advancing to Pizhan, more than three hundred Muslims surrendered the city; the army then joined Funinggan at Ulan Usu and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Pizhan more than three hundred Muslims surrendered the town; he rejoined Funinggan at Ulan Usu and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六十年，上命率師進取吐魯番，因留駐其地。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year the Emperor ordered him to lead troops to take Turfan and remained to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year (1721) he was ordered to take Turfan and stayed to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 策妄阿喇布坦來犯，阿喇納行與遇。

translations.literal: Tsewang Arabtan came to attack and met Ala'na on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Tsewang Arabtan attacked and met Ala'na on the march.

sentences.zh: 令分兵為三，突入陣，策妄阿喇布坦敗入林中，棄馬步戰，我師發槍擊殺準噶爾兵百餘，乃敗走，逐北數十里，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: He ordered the army divided into three columns to burst into the enemy formation. Tsewang Arabtan was beaten into the woods, abandoned his horses and fought on foot; our troops fired guns and killed more than a hundred Dzungar soldiers; the enemy then fled in defeat. Pursuing north for several tens of li, they took many captives and booty.
translations.idiomatic: He split his force into three columns and charged the enemy line. Tsewang Arabtan was driven into the woods, fought on foot after abandoning his horses, and lost more than a hundred Dzungars to musket fire before fleeing. The pursuit ran north for miles with heavy captures.

sentences.zh: 授協理將軍，築城屯墾，為持久計。

translations.literal: He was appointed assistant general, built walled towns and opened fields, and planned for a long campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was made assistant general, built towns and farms, and prepared for a long war.

sentences.zh: 阿喇納久居邊塞，悉敵情，疏請進兵伊犁。

translations.literal: Ala'na had long lived on the frontier and knew the enemy; he memorialized asking to advance on Ili.
translations.idiomatic: Long service on the frontier taught Ala'na the enemy's ways; he asked to march on Ili.

sentences.zh: 下議政大臣議，以賊已遠竄，暫緩進兵。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the deliberative ministers, who held that the rebels had already fled far and advance should be postponed.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberative ministers ruled that the foe had fled too far and advance should wait.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，擢鑲紅旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was promoted to Mongol deputy commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng (1723) he became Mongol deputy commander of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 師徵青海，命率兵二千駐布隆吉爾。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned in Qinghai he was ordered to lead two thousand troops to garrison Bulongji'er.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qinghai campaign he garrisoned Bulongji'er with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 賊酋阿喇布坦蘇巴泰來襲，遣師追至推默爾，大敗之。

translations.literal: The rebel chief Arabtan Subutai came to attack; he sent troops in pursuit to Tuimo'er and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel chief Arabtan Subutai attacked, he pursued him to Tuimo'er and routed him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Before long he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in camp.

sentences.zh: 遺疏為父請諡，上特許之。

translations.literal: In a death memorial he asked a posthumous title for his father; the Emperor specially granted it.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial asked a posthumous name for his father, and the Emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 賜白金千，遣官護喪歸，諡僖恪，加拜他喇布勒哈番，以其子伍彌泰兼襲，合為三等伯。

translations.literal: He was granted one thousand taels of silver, officials were sent to escort the coffin home, and he was given the posthumous title Xike, advanced to baitalaburuhan; his son Wumitai inherited jointly, combined as third-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: He received a thousand taels of silver, an escorted funeral, the posthumous name Xike, and advancement to baitalaburuhan; his son Wumitai inherited jointly as a third-class baron.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，定封號曰誠毅。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign the peerage was fixed as Chengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong the peerage was fixed as Chengyi.

sentences.zh: 伍彌泰自有傳。

translations.literal: Wumitai has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wumitai has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 吉勒塔布，李佳氏，滿洲正紅旗人，覺善第三子。

translations.literal: Jileitabu, of the Jiagiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner and the third son of Jueshan.
translations.idiomatic: Jileitabu, of the Jiagiya clan and the Plain Red Banner, was Jueshan's third son.

sentences.zh: 初授侍衛兼前鋒參領。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a guardsman and concurrently a vanguard adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a guardsman and vanguard adjutant.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，授正紅旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi he was appointed Mongol deputy commander-in-chief of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kangxi (1672) he became Mongol deputy commander of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿精忠叛，命偕副都統拉哈率師駐江寧。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rebelled; he was ordered, together with Deputy Commander Laha, to lead troops to garrison Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1674), when Geng Jingzhong rebelled, he and Deputy Commander Laha garrisoned Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 尋令援浙江。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to relieve Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to reinforce Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 從將軍貝子傅喇塔攻嵊縣，與精忠將曾養性等戰於黃瑞山，督兵乘夜分兩翼衝擊；

translations.literal: He followed Prince Beile Fulata in attacking Sheng County, fought Geng Jingzhong's general Zeng Yangxing and others at Huangruishan, and directed troops to strike in two wings by night;
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Beile Fulata against Sheng County, fought Zeng Yangxing at Huangruishan, and led a night attack in two wings;

sentences.zh: 又遣兵循山麓疾上，以鳥槍旁擊之，養性敗潰​​，克仙居。

translations.literal: he also sent troops swiftly up along the mountain foot and struck them from the flank with muskets; Yangxing was routed and Xianju was taken.
translations.idiomatic: he sent men racing along the foothills to flank them with muskets. Yangxing was routed and Xianju fell.

sentences.zh: 十四年，養性與叛將祖弘勳犯台州，吉勒塔布與都統沃申赴援，戰於平山嶺，殪賊四千餘；

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Yangxing, with the rebel general Zu Hongxun, invaded Taizhou. Jileitabu and Commander Woshen went to relieve them, fought at Pingshanling, and killed more than four thousand rebels;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Yangxing and the rebel Zu Hongxun struck Taizhou. Jileitabu and Commander Woshen relieved the city at Pingshanling and killed more than four thousand rebels;

sentences.zh: 奪梁蓬隘道，遇賊伏，盡殲之。

translations.literal: they seized the Liangpeng pass road, met an ambush, and annihilated it.
translations.idiomatic: they took the Liangpeng pass, met an ambush, and wiped it out.

sentences.zh: 直趨黃岩，副都統穆赫林督兵夾擊，養性夜走溫州。

translations.literal: Pressing straight on Huangyan, Deputy Commander Muhelin directed troops in a pincer; Yangxing fled by night to Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed on to Huangyan; Deputy Commander Muhelin struck from both sides, and Yangxing fled by night to Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 克黃岩，复戰於上塘嶺。

translations.literal: Huangyan was taken and they fought again at Shangtangling.
translations.idiomatic: They took Huangyan and fought again at Shangtangling.

sentences.zh: 攻溫州，久未下。

translations.literal: They attacked Wenzhou but could not take it for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Wenzhou dragged on.

sentences.zh: 十五年，養性復以四萬餘人來犯，吉勒塔布遣兵分道逆擊。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Yangxing again came to attack with more than forty thousand men; Jileitabu sent troops on separate roads to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Yangxing returned with more than forty thousand men; Jileitabu met him on several roads.

sentences.zh: 進剿處州，過三角嶺，循江度師。

translations.literal: Advancing to suppress Chuzhou, they passed Sanjiaoling and led the army across the river along its bank.
translations.idiomatic: Marching against Chuzhou they crossed Sanjiaoling and ferried the army along the river.

sentences.zh: 養性以百餘舟屯江上，陸兵屯得胜山下，據險拒我師。

translations.literal: Yangxing stationed more than a hundred boats on the river and land troops below Desheng Mountain, holding difficult ground to block our army.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing lined more than a hundred boats on the river and held Desheng Mountain with land troops.

sentences.zh: 吉勒塔布與總兵陳世凱分道拔賊壘，又以砲擊賊舟，沉諸江。

translations.literal: Jileitabu and Regional Commander Chen Shikai took rebel stockades on separate routes and also bombarded rebel boats and sank them in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jileitabu and Regional Commander Chen Shikai stormed rebel forts on separate routes and sank their boats with artillery.

sentences.zh: 師次溫溪渡口，擊敗精忠將馬成龍等，斬千餘級，遂與康親王師會衢州。

translations.literal: The army halted at Wenxi ford, defeated Geng Jingzhong's generals Ma Chenglong and others, beheaded more than a thousand, and then joined Prince Kang's army at Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenxi ford they defeated Ma Chenglong and other rebel generals, took more than a thousand heads, and joined Prince Kang at Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 偕都統賚塔等擊精忠將馬九玉，戰於大溪灘。

translations.literal: Together with Commander Saibao and others he attacked Geng Jingzhong's general Ma Jiuyu and fought at Daxitan.
translations.idiomatic: With Commander Saibao he attacked Ma Jiuyu at Daxitan.

sentences.zh: 吉勒塔布督兵逾三濠，進焚木城，克江山，九玉敗遁。

translations.literal: Jileitabu directed troops over three ditches, advanced to burn the wooden wall, took Jiangshan, and Jiuyu fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Jileitabu crossed three trenches, burned the wooden fort, took Jiangshan, and Jiuyu fled.

sentences.zh: 遂度仙霞嶺，進克浦城、建陽諸縣。

translations.literal: He then crossed Xianxialing and advanced to take Pucheng, Jianyang, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Xianxialing and took Pucheng, Jianyang, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 從康親王進次福州，精忠降。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Kang to advance and halt at Fuzhou, and Geng Jingzhong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Kang to Fuzhou, where Geng Jingzhong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擊鄭錦同安。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he attacked Zheng Jing at Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1677) he attacked Zheng Jing at Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 十八年，與錦將劉國軒戰於下坑、於歐溪頭、於郭坑，皆勝，斬二千餘級，收海澄。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he fought Zheng Jing's general Liu Guoxuan at Xiakeng, at Ouxitou, and at Guokeng—all victories—and beheaded more than two thousand, recovering Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1679) he beat Liu Guoxuan at Xiakeng, Ouxitou, and Guokeng, took more than two thousand heads, and recovered Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 與沃申駐師漳州。

translations.literal: He and Woshen garrisoned the army at Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He and Woshen garrisoned Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，師還，累擢護軍統領、正紅旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the army returned; he was promoted step by step to guards commander-in-chief and Mongol commander-in-chief of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1682) the army withdrew; he rose to guards commander-in-chief and Mongol commander of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，授兵部尚書，列議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed Minister of War and made a deliberative minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1688) he became Minister of War and a deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹侵喀爾喀，上命吉勒塔布與都統巴海等徵科爾沁諸部兵備邊。

translations.literal: When Galdan invaded the Khalkha, the Emperor ordered Jileitabu, together with Commander Bahai and others, to levy Khorchin troops for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Galdan invaded the Khalkha, the Emperor ordered Jileitabu and Commander Bahai to raise Khorchin troops for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 尋命往蘇尼特，度水草佳處為喀爾喀牧地。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to go to the Sunid and choose good pasture and water as Khalkha grazing land.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to the Sunid to choose pasture for the Khalkha.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，命與尚書阿喇尼出塞，自歸化至圖拉置台站，率師會喀爾喀諸部，自洮瀨河進攻噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was ordered, with Minister Arani, to go beyond the passes, establish courier stations from Guihua to Tula, lead troops to join the Khalkha tribes, and advance against Galdan from the Taolai River.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1690) he and Minister Arani went beyond the passes, set up stations from Guihua to Tula, joined the Khalkha, and advanced on Galdan from the Taolai River.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹掠烏珠穆秦部，至烏勒輝河，我師與遇，分兵乘夜挑戰。

translations.literal: Galdan plundered the Ujumchin tribe and reached the Wulehui River; our army met him and sent troops to challenge by night.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan raided the Ujumchin and reached the Wulehui River; our forces met him with night attacks.

sentences.zh: 喀爾喀兵違節度，亂陣，戰失利。

translations.literal: Khalkha troops disobeyed orders and threw the line into disorder; the battle was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Khalkha troops broke discipline, the line collapsed, and the battle was lost.

sentences.zh: 吉勒塔布當奪官，命留佐領，率兵駐呼魯固爾河。

translations.literal: Jileitabu should have been stripped of office; he was ordered to retain his company command and lead troops to garrison the Hulugu'er River.
translations.idiomatic: He should have lost his post but was kept as company commander and stationed on the Hulugu'er River.

sentences.zh: 旋命與內大臣阿密達同駐克勒，待裕親王師至，分三隊以進。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered, together with Interior Minister Amida, to garrison at Kele and wait until Prince Yu's army arrived, then advance in three columns.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon paired with Interior Minister Amida at Kele to await Prince Yu and advance in three columns.

sentences.zh: 吉勒塔佈為第一隊，大敗噶爾丹於烏闌布通。

translations.literal: Jileitabu was the first column and inflicted a great defeat on Galdan at Ulan Butung.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the first column, he routed Galdan at Ulan Butung.

sentences.zh: 三十年，詔移喀爾喀土謝圖、車臣兩部歸附人牧近邊。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year an edict moved the surrendered people of the Khalkha Tushiyetu and Chechen khans to graze near the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1691) surrendered Khalkha of the Tushiyetu and Chechen khans were moved to border pastures.

sentences.zh: 上出塞撫綏，令吉勒塔布與尚書馬齊、班第等，先期集歸附人於上都河、額爾屯河以待。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went beyond the passes to reassure them, he ordered Jileitabu, together with Minister Maqi, Bandi, and others, to gather the surrendered people beforehand at the Shangdu and Erten rivers to await him.
translations.idiomatic: On the Emperor's frontier tour he told Jileitabu, Minister Maqi, and Bandi to assemble the surrendered Khalkha at the Shangdu and Erten rivers beforehand.

sentences.zh: 上慮巴圖爾額爾克濟農掠喀爾喀，命吉勒塔布督喀爾喀諸部兵為備。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared Batuer Erkejin might plunder the Khalkha and ordered Jileitabu to direct Khalkha troops as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Batuer Erkejin might raid the Khalkha, the Emperor had Jileitabu ready Khalkha forces.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，巴圖爾額爾克濟農降，罷兵歸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Batuer Erkejin surrendered and the troops returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year (1692) Batuer Erkejin surrendered and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，擢都統。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was promoted to commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year (1696) he was made commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he died and was granted funeral honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year (1697) he died and received funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 殷化行，字熙如，陝西咸陽人。

translations.literal: Yin Huaxing, style Xiru, was a native of Xianyang, Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Huaxing, courtesy name Xiru, was from Xianyang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初以王姓成康熙九年武進士。

translations.literal: At first, under the surname Wang, he passed the military jinshi examination in the ninth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Originally surnamed Wang, he passed the military jinshi in the ninth year of Kangxi (1670).

sentences.zh: 十三年，從經略莫洛討吳三桂，授守備。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed Commissioner-general Moluo against Wu Sangui and was appointed a garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1674) he followed Moluo against Wu Sangui and became a garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 會王輔臣叛，莫洛遇害，化行被脅羈秦州，稱病不為賊用。

translations.literal: When Wang Fuchen rebelled, Moluo was killed; Huaxing was coerced and held at Qinzhou, feigning illness and refusing to serve the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Fuchen rebelled and Moluo was killed, Huaxing was held at Qinzhou, feigned illness, and refused to serve the rebels.

sentences.zh: 逾年，自拔歸，總督哈佔奏復原職，補火器營守備。

translations.literal: After more than a year he escaped and returned; Governor Hazhan memorialized restoration of his former post and he was made garrison commander of the Firearms Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he escaped home; Governor Hazhan restored his rank and he joined the Firearms Brigade.

sentences.zh: 從振武將軍佛尼勒戰牛頭山，攻克上、下嶺。

translations.literal: He followed Pacification General Fonil in fighting at Niutoushan and captured Upper and Lower Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Pacification General Fonil at Niutoushan and took Upper and Lower Ling.

sentences.zh: 三桂將王屏籓據漢中，以二萬人犯寶雞。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's general Wang Pingfan held Hanzhong and invaded Baoji with twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's general Wang Pingfan held Hanzhong and struck Baoji with twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 大將軍圖海檄化行赴援，破敵，解西山堡圍。

translations.literal: Grand General Tuhai ordered Huaxing to relieve them; he broke the enemy and lifted the siege of Xishan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Tuhai sent Huaxing to relieve Baoji; he routed the enemy and lifted the siege of Xishan Fort.

sentences.zh: 復自大泥峪取兩河關，復興安州城。

translations.literal: He again took Lianghe Pass from Dani Valley and recovered Xing'an prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: From Dani Valley he retook Lianghe Pass and recovered Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 十九年，佛尼勒援永寧，化行為前鋒，敗敵托川，擊走三桂將胡國柱於安寧橋。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Fonil relieved Yongning; Huaxing was vanguard, defeated the enemy at Tuochuan, and drove off Wu Sangui's general Hu Guozhu at Anning Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year (1680) he was Fonil's vanguard at Yongning, beat the foe at Tuochuan, and drove off Hu Guozhu at Anning Bridge.

sentences.zh: 調援敘州，與西寧總兵李芳述守城，賊分三路來攻，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Transferred to relieve Xuzhou, he and Xining Regional Commander Li Fangshu defended the city; the rebels attacked on three roads and were repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Xuzhou, he and Li Fangshu held the city against a three-pronged assault and beat it back.

sentences.zh: 圖海、哈佔合疏陳化行奮戰狀，特擢漢中城守營副將。

translations.literal: Tuhai and Hazhan jointly memorialized Huaxing's fierce fighting; he was specially promoted to deputy commander of the Hanzhong garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhai and Hazhan praised his fighting; he was promoted to deputy commander at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 二十年，逐國柱，迭戰安邊、敘馬、連峰、石盤關諸處，屢克要隘，复馬湖府城。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he pursued Guozhu, fought repeatedly at Anbian, Xuma, Lianfeng, Shipanguan, and other places, repeatedly took key passes, and recovered Mahu prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1681) he pursued Guozhu through Anbian, Xuma, Lianfeng, and Shipanguan, took key passes, and recovered Mahu.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，追議輔臣叛時被脅，坐奪官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, reviewing coercion during Fuchen's rebellion, he was punished by removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (1683) a review of his coercion under Fuchen cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 哈佔以化行未為輔臣用，從征有勞，奏復原職，授直隸三屯營副將。

translations.literal: Hazhan held that Huaxing had not served Fuchen and had merit on campaign; he memorialized restoration of his former post and appointment as deputy commander of the Santunying in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan argued he had never served Fuchen and had campaign merit; he was restored and made deputy commander at Santunying in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，敘功加一等，授都司僉書，兼管副將事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, for recorded merit, he was advanced one grade and appointed assistant regional commander while continuing to perform deputy commander duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1684) merit raised him one grade to assistant regional commander with deputy duties.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，上幸畿東，化行扈從行圍，賜上用佩刀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, when the Emperor visited eastern Ji, Huaxing attended the hunt and was given the Emperor's own waist sword.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year (1686) he attended the eastern hunt and received the Emperor's own sword.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢福建台灣總兵，賜貂裘、白金。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to regional commander of Taiwan in Fujian and given a sable coat and silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year (1687) he became Fujian regional commander at Taiwan and received a sable coat and silver.

sentences.zh: 時議城台灣，化行言地皆浮沙，難以鞏固，令部下人致樹一，植為城，數日而成。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of walling Taiwan; Huaxing said the ground was all drifting sand and hard to consolidate, so he had a subordinate bring a tree, plant it as a wall, and in a few days it was done.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated fortifying Taiwan he said the sand would not hold stone; he had a tree planted as a wall and in days it stood.

sentences.zh: 諸部亦各植木城，繕治甲兵，防禦以固。

translations.literal: Each department likewise planted wooden walls, repaired arms and armor, and strengthened defense.
translations.idiomatic: Other units copied the wooden walls, repaired arms, and tightened defense.

sentences.zh: 三十年，移襄陽。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was transferred to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1691) he moved to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 陝西旱，米價騰貴，民多流移。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered drought; grain prices soared and many people drifted away.
translations.idiomatic: Drought in Shaanxi sent grain prices soaring and drove many people away.

sentences.zh: 詔發襄陽米二萬石水運至商州，改陸運至西安。

translations.literal: An edict sent twenty thousand shi of grain from Xiangyang by water to Shangzhou, then overland to Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: The court shipped twenty thousand shi from Xiangyang by water to Shangzhou, then overland to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 命內閣學士德珠與化行及總督丁思孔往督水陸輓運，並護流民還裡。

translations.literal: Academician Dezhu was ordered, together with Huaxing and Governor Ding Sikong, to supervise transport by land and water and escort displaced people home.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Dezhu, Huaxing, and Governor Ding Sikong supervised transport and escorted refugees home.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，移登州。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was transferred to Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year (1693) he was moved to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 复移寧夏。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He was then moved to Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，三路出師，發陝西兵當西路，遣刑部尚書圖納會將軍、督、撫及河西提、鎮議進兵事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year the Emperor campaigned in person against Galdan; three columns marched out. Shaanxi troops formed the western route. Minister of Justice Tuna was sent to meet generals, governors, and the Hexi commanders to discuss advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year (1696) the Emperor took the field against Galdan on three routes. Shaanxi troops formed the west; Minister Tuna met commanders to plan the advance.

sentences.zh: 化行陳方略，詔報可。

translations.literal: Huaxing set forth a plan; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaxing proposed a plan and the Emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 時綠旗兵統於振武將軍孫思克，率涼州總兵董大成、肅州總兵潘育龍及化行自寧夏出塞，會大將軍費揚古進剿。

translations.literal: Green Standard troops were then under Pacification General Sun Sike, who led Liangzhou Regional Commander Dong Dacheng, Suzhou Regional Commander Pan Yulong, and Huaxing out from Ningxia beyond the passes to join Grand General Fei Yanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Green Standards under Sun Sike marched from Ningxia with Dong Dacheng, Pan Yulong, and Huaxing to join Fei Yanggu.

sentences.zh: 化行領所部兵三千至翁金河，簡精卒前進，遇敵昭莫多。

translations.literal: Huaxing led three thousand of his troops to Wengjin River, chose elite men to advance, and met the enemy at Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: Huaxing led three thousand men to Wengjin River, picked elites, and met the enemy at Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 山崖峻削，其南漸纮，有小山橫亙，化行急據其巔，麾軍士畢登。

translations.literal: The cliffs were steep; to the south they sloped gently, and a small hill lay across the way. Huaxing hastened to seize its summit and ordered all soldiers up.
translations.idiomatic: Cliffs rose steeply; southward the slope eased and a hill barred the way. Huaxing seized the crest and got every man up.

sentences.zh: 敵猝至山腹，發砲擊之，噶爾丹率眾死鬥，鋒甚銳。

translations.literal: The enemy suddenly reached mid-slope; he opened fire. Galdan led his host in a desperate fight and their edge was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy rushed the slope; he opened fire. Galdan fought desperately and his line was fierce.

sentences.zh: 化行使告費揚古曰：「賊陣堅，宜遣一軍衝其脅，賊婦女輜重俱在後陣，劫之必亂。」

translations.literal: Huaxing sent word to Fei Yanggu: "The enemy line is solid; one force should strike their flank. Women and baggage are all in the rear; if we raid them they will surely fall into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Huaxing told Fei Yanggu the enemy line was tight and a flanking force should strike the rear where women and baggage lay—raiding them would break the formation.

sentences.zh: 費揚古從之。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) Fei Yanggu agreed.

sentences.zh: 化行望山下兩軍將薄陣，鼓行而下，敵披靡，死傷枕藉。

translations.literal: Huaxing saw the two armies below about to close; he beat the drums and marched down. The enemy collapsed; dead and wounded lay piled together.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the wings about to close below, he drummed his men downhill. The enemy broke; dead and wounded covered the field.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹敗遁，詔班師。

translations.literal: Galdan fled in defeat and an edict ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan fled and the army was ordered home.

sentences.zh: 是役化行功最。

translations.literal: In this campaign Huaxing's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In that fight Huaxing's merit stood first.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，疏請率兵二千至郭多里巴爾哈孫偵擒噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he memorialized asking to lead two thousand troops to Guodilibaerhasun to scout and capture Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year (1697) he asked to lead two thousand men to Guodilibaerhasun to hunt Galdan.

sentences.zh: 會上西巡，將幸寧夏，化行迎謁，奏請行圍花馬池觀軍容。

translations.literal: When the Emperor toured the west and was about to visit Ningxia, Huaxing met him and asked to hold a hunt at Huamachi to display the army.
translations.idiomatic: During the western tour he met the Emperor en route to Ningxia and asked to hunt at Huamachi to show the troops.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「師行賴馬力。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Campaigns depend on horse strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said campaigns depend on horse strength.

sentences.zh: 今噶爾丹未滅，寧夏兵至花馬池，往來七八日，馬必疲。

translations.literal: Galdan is not yet destroyed. If Ningxia troops go to Huamachi and back in seven or eight days, the horses will surely be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan was not yet destroyed; a round trip from Ningxia to Huamachi in seven or eight days would exhaust the horses.

sentences.zh: 獵細事耳，罷獵而休馬，以獵噶爾丹何如？」

translations.literal: Hunting is a small matter. Cease the hunt and rest the horses—how about hunting Galdan instead?"
translations.idiomatic: Hunting was a small thing—better rest the horses and hunt Galdan instead.

sentences.zh: 乃令化行率所部兵五百人從昭武將軍馬思喀復出塞。

translations.literal: He then ordered Huaxing to lead five hundred of his troops to follow Pacification General Masika again beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) He ordered Huaxing to take five hundred men and follow Pacification General Masika beyond the passes again.

sentences.zh: 尋命化行參贊軍務，諭謂綠旗總兵官未有授參贊者，並賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to serve on staff; the Emperor said no Green Standard regional commander had yet been given staff rank, and he was also granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made staff officer—the first Green Standard regional commander so honored—and given a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 師次郭多里巴爾哈孫，會大將軍費揚古兵。

translations.literal: The army halted at Guodilibaerhasun and joined Grand General Fei Yanggu's force.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Guodilibaerhasun and joined Fei Yanggu.

sentences.zh: 進至洪郭羅阿濟爾罕，噶爾丹死，詔班師。

translations.literal: Advancing to Honggeluoajierhan, they learned Galdan was dead and an edict ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: At Honggeluoajierhan they learned Galdan was dead and were ordered home.

sentences.zh: 化行還寧夏。

translations.literal: Huaxing returned to Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Huaxing returned to Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，請復本姓。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he asked to resume his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year (1698) he asked to resume his birth surname.

sentences.zh: 敘昭莫多功，予拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: For merit at Jao Modo he was granted the hereditary rank of tosaha.
translations.idiomatic: For Jao Modo he received a hereditary tosaha rank.

sentences.zh: 擢廣東提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial commander of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He became provincial commander of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，瓊州營游擊詹伯豸等擾黎人，黎人王鎮邦為亂，以化行約束不嚴，降級留任。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year Regional Commander Zhan Bozhi and others of the Qiongzhou garrison harassed the Li; the Li leader Wang Zhenbang rose in revolt. Because Huaxing had not kept strict control, he was demoted but kept in post.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year (1700) Qiongzhou troops harassed the Li and Wang Zhenbang rebelled; lax control cost Huaxing a demotion but not his post.

sentences.zh: 四十年，連、陽瑤為亂，裡入峒、油嶺二排尤凶橫。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year the Yao of Lian and Yang rebelled; the Li Ru Dong and You Ling two pai were especially fierce.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year (1701) the Yao of Lian and Yang rebelled, above all the Li Ru Dong and You Ling communities.

sentences.zh: 化行率總兵劉虎駐師裡入峒，遣副將林芳入排，使執為亂者以獻。

translations.literal: Huaxing led Regional Commander Liu Hu to garrison Li Ru Dong, sent Deputy Commander Lin Fang into the pai, and had the rebels seized and handed over.
translations.idiomatic: Huaxing and Liu Hu held Li Ru Dong while Deputy Lin Fang entered the community to seize the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 瑤人戕芳及所從兵役。

translations.literal: The Yao killed Fang and the soldiers who followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao killed Fang and his escort.

sentences.zh: 上命尚書嵩祝為將軍，令化行及廣西、湖南提督各發兵討之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Minister Songzhu as general and told Huaxing and the provincial commanders of Guangxi and Hunan each to send troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Minister Songzhu general and ordered Huaxing and the Guangxi and Hunan commanders to march.

sentences.zh: 四十一年夏，會師連州，分扼要隘，瑤人懼，縛獻為亂者李貴、鄧二等，置諸法，餘悉就撫。

translations.literal: In the summer of the forty-first year the armies met at Lianzhou, held key passes, and the Yao, in fear, bound and handed over the rebels Li Gui, Deng Er, and others, who were punished by law; the rest were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the forty-first year (1702) allied forces held the passes; the Yao surrendered Li Gui, Deng Er, and other ringleaders for execution and the rest submitted.

sentences.zh: 尋追按芳被戕，化行、虎不能救，虎奪官，化行休致。

translations.literal: Soon, reviewing Fang's killing, it was held that Huaxing and Hu could not save him; Hu was stripped of office and Huaxing retired.
translations.idiomatic: A review of Fang's death found Huaxing and Hu could not save him; Hu lost his post and Huaxing retired.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上幸西安，化行迎謁，授其子純四等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, when the Emperor visited Xi'an, Huaxing met him and his son Chun was appointed a fourth-class guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year (1703), when the Emperor visited Xi'an, Huaxing met him and his son Chun became a fourth-class guardsman.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year (1710) he died.

sentences.zh: 潘育龍，字飛天，甘肅靖遠人。

translations.literal: Pan Yulong, style Feitian, was a native of Jingyuan, Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yulong, courtesy name Feitian, was from Jingyuan in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 初入伍，從征李來亨等於茅麓山，有功。

translations.literal: At first he enlisted and followed campaigns against Li Laiheng and others at Maolushan with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted and fought Li Laiheng at Maolushan with distinction.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，王輔臣叛，育龍從副將偏圖攻三水、淳化，復從揚威將軍阿密達戰涇州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi, when Wang Fuchen rebelled, Yulong followed Vice Commander Biantu in attacking Sanshui and Chunhua and again followed Pacification General Amida in fighting at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1675), when Wang Fuchen rebelled, he followed Biantu at Sanshui and Chunhua and Amida at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 寧夏道梗，大將軍董額使育龍赴提督陳福軍，自紅河川、白馬城諸要隘轉戰七晝夜，達寧夏。

translations.literal: The Ningxia road was blocked; Grand General Dong E sent Yulong to Provincial Commander Chen Fu's army. From Honghechuan, Baimacheng, and other key points he fought for seven days and nights and reached Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: With Ningxia cut off, Grand General Dong E sent him to Chen Fu; he fought seven days and nights through Honghechuan and Baimacheng to reach Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 駐靈州，招撫散卒。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Lingzhou and gathered scattered soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He held Lingzhou and gathered scattered troops.

sentences.zh: 總督哈佔調援山陽，敗賊於甘溝口。

translations.literal: Governor Hazhan transferred him to relieve Shanyang and defeated rebels at Gangoukou.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Hazhan sent him to Shanyang, where he beat rebels at Gangoukou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從撫遠大將軍圖海奪平涼城北虎山墩。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief Tuhai in taking Hushandun north of Pingliang city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1676) he followed Tuhai in taking Hushandun north of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 累擢守備。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 十七年，吳三桂兵犯牛頭山、香泉，育龍從總兵王好問等出間道擊破之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Wu Sangui's troops attacked Niutoushan and Xiangquan; Yulong followed Regional Commander Wang Haowen and others by a hidden road and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1678) he helped Wang Haowen repel Wu Sangui at Niutoushan and Xiangquan by a hidden route.

sentences.zh: 十八年，克梁河關，斬三桂將李景才、景文略等；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he took Lianghe Pass and beheaded Wu Sangui's generals Li Jingcai, Jing Wenlue, and others;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1679) he took Lianghe Pass and killed Wu Sangui's generals Li Jingcai and Jing Wenlue;

sentences.zh: 薄興安，三桂將謝泗、王永世以城降。

translations.literal: pressing on Xing'an, Wu Sangui's generals Xie Si and Wang Yongshi surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: then pressed Xing'an until Xie Si and Wang Yongshi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 敘功，擢都司僉書。

translations.literal: For recorded merit he was promoted to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Merit made him assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 叛將譚弘據川東，育龍從哈佔進剿，復大竹、渠縣。

translations.literal: The rebel Tan Hong held eastern Sichuan; Yulong followed Hazhan in suppression and recovered Dazhu and Quxian.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan Hong held eastern Sichuan he followed Hazhan and recovered Dazhu and Quxian.

sentences.zh: 遷游擊。

translations.literal: He was transferred to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: He became a brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以總督噶思泰薦，擢甘州副將。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, on Governor Gasi Tai's recommendation, he was promoted to deputy commander of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1688), on Gasi Tai's recommendation, he became Ganzhou deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 學士達瑚等自西藏使旋，至嘉峪關外，為西海阿奇羅卜藏所掠。

translations.literal: Academician Dahu and others returning from a mission to Tibet were plundered beyond Jiayuguan by Aqiluobuzang of the Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Dahu's party returning from Tibet was robbed beyond Jiayuguan by Aqiluobuzang of the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 將軍孫思克使育龍偕游擊韓成等搗其巢，斬級四百有奇，阿奇羅卜藏遁。

translations.literal: General Sun Sike sent Yulong with Brigade Commander Han Cheng and others to strike their nest, cut off more than four hundred heads, and Aqiluobuzang fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sike sent Yulong with Han Cheng to raid their camp, took more than four hundred heads, and Aqiluobuzang fled.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 三十年，赴寧夏防剿噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he went to Ningxia to guard against and suppress Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1691) he went to Ningxia against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 時改肅州協為鎮，即以育龍為總兵。

translations.literal: At the time the Suzhou command was changed to a garrison; Yulong was made regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzhou became a garrison he was made its regional commander.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，降番罕篤與羅卜藏額林臣、奇齊克等復叛，育龍追至庫列圖嶺，斬四十餘級，獲百二十人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the surrendered tribesman Handu, Lobuzang Elinchen, Qiqike, and others rebelled again; Yulong pursued to Kulietu Ridge, beheaded more than forty, and captured one hundred twenty men.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year (1692) Handu, Lobuzang Elinchen, and Qiqike rebelled; he pursued to Kulietu Ridge, killed forty, and took one hundred twenty prisoners.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，噶爾丹屬回塔什蘭和卓等五百餘人入犯，渡三岔河，育龍擊擒之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year more than five hundred followers of Galdan, Muslim Tashilanhezhuo and others, invaded, crossed the Sancha River, and Yulong attacked and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year (1695) five hundred of Galdan's Muslims under Tashilanhezhuo crossed the Sancha River; Yulong captured them.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從征噶爾丹，遇賊昭莫多，飛砲中育龍右頤，益力戰，賊敗遁。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he followed the campaign against Galdan, met the enemy at Jao Modo; a cannonball struck Yulong's right cheek, yet he fought harder and the enemy fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year (1696) at Jao Modo a shell struck his right cheek; he fought on harder and the enemy fled.

sentences.zh: 師還，召至京師，上撫視其創，命御醫診視，賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was summoned to the capital; the Emperor caressed his wound, ordered the imperial physician to treat him, and gave him a suit of clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the capital, he was tended by the imperial physician, given a suit of clothes, and the Emperor examined his wound.

sentences.zh: 移鎮天津。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 敘功，予拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the hereditary rank of tosaha.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received a hereditary tosaha rank.

sentences.zh: 四十年，擢陝西提督，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted to provincial commander of Shaanxi and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year (1701) he became Shaanxi provincial commander with a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上西巡，育龍迎謁山西，賜御書榜。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, when the Emperor toured the west, Yulong met him in Shanxi and was given an imperial inscription board.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year (1703), during the western tour, he met the Emperor in Shanxi and received an imperial plaque.

sentences.zh: 駐蹕渭南，閱固原將卒校射，顧大學士馬齊等曰：「朕巡歷諸省，綠旗無如潘育龍兵者。」

translations.literal: Halting at Weinan, he reviewed the archery of Guyuan officers and soldiers and turned to Grand Secretary Maqi and others, saying: "In all the provinces I have toured, no Green Standard troops equal Pan Yulong's."
translations.idiomatic: At Weinan he reviewed Guyuan archery and told Grand Secretary Maqi that in all his tours no Green Standards matched Pan Yulong's men.

sentences.zh: 命加秩。

translations.literal: He ordered his rank raised.
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) His rank was raised.

sentences.zh: 尋特授鎮綏將軍，領提督如故。

translations.literal: He was soon specially appointed Pacification General while retaining his provincial command.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Pacification General while keeping his provincial post.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，上幸五台，育龍迎謁，賞賚優渥，親制詩章寵之。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, when the Emperor visited Wutai, Yulong met him, was richly rewarded, and the Emperor personally composed a poem in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year (1710), at Wutai, he was richly rewarded and honored with an imperial poem.

sentences.zh: 時有陳四等率妻子遊行鬻技，走馬上竿，鵕索算卦，俗名曰卦子。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Si and others led wives and children traveling to sell skills—performing on horseback, pole-climbing, rope-walking, and fortune-telling—commonly called guazi.
translations.idiomatic: Then Chen Si and others toured with families selling stunts—horsemanship, pole acts, rope tricks, and divination—known as guazi.

sentences.zh: 人既眾，遂為盜。

translations.literal: When crowds gathered they turned to banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds drew bandits.

sentences.zh: 育龍捕得五百九十餘人。

translations.literal: Yulong captured more than five hundred ninety of them.
translations.idiomatic: Yulong seized more than five hundred ninety of them.

sentences.zh: 有司讞鞫，因疏請飭各省督撫責所屬鄉村堡寨，遇令改業，編戶為民，給荒地開墾，馬騾牲畜變為牛種，載入賦役全書。

translations.literal: The officials tried the cases; he therefore memorialized asking that governors and governors-general instruct village stockades under them that when such people were encountered they should be made to change trades, registered as commoners, given wasteland to open, horses and mules converted to oxen for seed, and entered in the tax register.
translations.idiomatic: After trial he asked governors to register such performers as farmers, give them wasteland, replace horses with oxen, and enter them in the tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved and implemented it.

sentences.zh: 尋以病累疏乞休，詔輒慰留。

translations.literal: Soon, repeatedly memorializing illness to request retirement, he received edicts of consolation and retention.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated illness memorials brought edicts urging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，卒，贈太子少保，賜祭葬，諡襄勇。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he died, was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted funeral honors, and given the posthumous title Xiangyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year (1719) he died, was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent posthumously, and received funeral honors and the name Xiangyong.

sentences.zh: 孫紹週，改籍陝西西安。

translations.literal: Sun Shaozhou changed his registration to Xi'an, Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shaozhou shifted his household register to Xi'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 襲世職，授二等侍衛。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary office and was appointed a second-class guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the family rank and became a second-class guardsman.

sentences.zh: 累遷廣西慶遠協副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to deputy commander of the Qingyuan command in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deputy commander at Qingyuan in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，總督鄂爾泰奏開古州、都江河道，以定旦、來牛二寨苗梗路，檄紹週統廣西兵赴古州諸葛營，與貴州副將趙文英會剿，盡平賊寨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng, Governor Ortai memorialized opening the Guzhou and Duojiang river routes; the Miao of Dingdan and Lainiu villages blocked the road. An order went to Shaozhou to lead Guangxi troops to the Zhuge camp at Guzhou and, with Guizhou Deputy Commander Zhao Wenying, join in suppression and level all rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng, Governor Ortai opened the Guzhou and Duojiang routes; Miao at Dingdan and Lainiu blocked them. Shaozhou led Guangxi troops to Zhuge camp, joined Zhao Wenying, and leveled the rebel forts.

sentences.zh: 擢雲南提督，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial commander of Yunnan and granted a flowered feather.
translations.idiomatic: He became Yunnan provincial commander with a flowered feather.

sentences.zh: 調古北口，以病解任。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gubeikou and resigned because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Gubeikou and resigned for illness.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Qianlong (1753) he died.

sentences.zh: 高宗追念育龍軍功，特予恩騎尉世職，以紹周子忱嗣。

translations.literal: Gaozong, recalling Yulong's military merit, specially granted the hereditary rank of enjiwei, inherited by Shaozhou's son Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor, remembering Yulong's service, granted an enjiwei hereditary rank to Shaozhou's son Chen.

sentences.zh: 之善，育龍從孫，仍籍甘肅靖遠。

translations.literal: Zhishan was Yulong's grandnephew and remained registered at Jingyuan, Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishan, Yulong's grandnephew, remained registered at Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初從育龍徵噶爾丹。

translations.literal: At first he followed Yulong against Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: He first campaigned with Yulong against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 昭莫多之役，力戰中槍，詔來京師醫治。

translations.literal: At Jao Modo he fought hard and was shot; an edict ordered him brought to the capital for treatment.
translations.idiomatic: At Jao Modo he was shot in hard fighting and was ordered to Beijing for care.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上幸西安，之善迎謁臨潼，授藍翎侍衛，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, when the Emperor visited Xi'an, Zhishan met him at Lintong, was appointed a blue-lance guardsman, and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year (1703) he met the Emperor at Lintong, became a blue-lance guardsman, and received a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 補肅州鎮標游擊。

translations.literal: He was made brigade commander of the Suzhou garrison detachment.
translations.idiomatic: He became brigade commander of the Suzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 策妄阿喇布坦以二千人侵哈密，之善率兵二百擊敗之。

translations.literal: Tsewang Arabtan invaded Hami with two thousand men; Zhishan led two hundred troops and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Tsewang Arabtan invaded Hami with two thousand men; Zhishan beat him with two hundred.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其勇，超擢陝西潼關副將。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his courage and promoted him in one step to deputy commander of Tongguan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his courage and jumped him to Tongguan deputy commander in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 從靖逆將軍富寧安擊準噶爾於烏魯木齊，多俘獲。

translations.literal: He followed Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief Funinggan in striking the Dzungars at Urumqi and took many captives.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Funinggan against the Dzungars at Urumqi with heavy captures.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，青海台吉羅卜藏丹津叛，侵布隆吉爾，與參將孫繼宗引兵夾擊，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng the Qinghai taiji Lobzang Danjin rebelled and invaded Bulongji'er; with Brigade Commander Sun Jizong he led troops in a pincer and killed and captured without number.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng, when Lobzang Danjin rebelled in Qinghai and struck Bulongji'er, he and Sun Jizong pincered the foe with countless kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 擢四川川北總兵，移鎮陝西西安。

translations.literal: He was promoted to regional commander of northern Sichuan and transferred to garrison Xi'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became northern Sichuan regional commander, then garrison commander at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 之善以邊外遼闊，當設卡路杜窺伺，乃遣兵於沙州西路伊遜察罕齊老圖及察罕烏蘇諾爾分路偵禦。

translations.literal: Zhishan held that the outer frontier was vast and card posts should be set to watch; he sent troops on the western road of Shazhou at Yixun Chahan Qilaotu and at Chahan Usu Nor on separate routes to scout and defend.
translations.idiomatic: He argued the frontier was vast and needed card posts, sending detachments west of Shazhou at Yixun Chahan Qilaotu and Chahan Usu Nor.

sentences.zh: 並以住牧熟夷數百戶，分置諸要隘，诇敵情，督修西安城及沙州五堡，以二千四百戶屯田沙州，籌牛種，建房舍。

translations.literal: He also placed several hundred settled tribesmen at key points to spy on the enemy, supervised repair of Xi'an city and the five forts of Shazhou, and settled twenty-four hundred households to farm at Shazhou, providing oxen and seed and building houses.
translations.idiomatic: He posted settled tribesmen at passes to watch the enemy, rebuilt Xi'an and Shazhou's five forts, and settled twenty-four hundred farming households at Shazhou with oxen, seed, and houses.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，上深嘉之，命署固原提督。

translations.literal: When his memorial was reported, the Emperor deeply praised it and ordered him to act as provincial commander of Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised the plan and made him acting Guyuan provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「此軍乃汝叔祖潘育龍所整理，為天下第一營伍，流風餘韻，至今可觀。

translations.literal: An edict said: "This army was organized by your granduncle Pan Yulong into the finest camp in the empire; its tradition can still be seen today.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said his granduncle Pan Yulong had made the finest camp in the empire and its spirit should still be visible.

sentences.zh: 若不能企及，何顏以對朕耶？」

translations.literal: If you cannot equal it, with what face can you answer Us?"
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot match it, how will you face Us?"

sentences.zh: 尋以目眚解任。

translations.literal: He was soon relieved because of eye disease.
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) He soon resigned with eye trouble.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1733) he died.

sentences.zh: 額倫特，科奇哩氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人，佛尼埒子也。

translations.literal: E'lunte, of the Keqiri clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner and son of Fonile.
translations.idiomatic: E'lunte, of the Keqiri clan and the Bordered Red Banner, was Fonile's son.

sentences.zh: 佛尼埒卒官，家貧不能還京。

translations.literal: When Fonile died in office the family was too poor to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Fonile died in office the family was too poor to return to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 四川總督哈佔請留額倫特西安效力，部議不許，上特允之。

translations.literal: Sichuan Governor Hazhan asked that E'lunte be kept to serve at Xi'an; the ministry deliberated and did not approve, but the Emperor specially allowed it.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Hazhan asked to keep E'lunte at Xi'an; the ministry refused but the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十三年，授西安駐防佐領。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi he was appointed company commander of the Xi'an garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi (1684) he became a Xi'an garrison company commander.

sentences.zh: 三十年，從將軍尼雅翰逐厄魯特巴圖爾額爾克濟農，又從將軍郎坦赴克錫圖額，皆有勞。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he followed General Niyahan in driving off the Eleuth Batuer Erkejin and again followed General Langtan to Kexitue with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1691) he followed Niyahan against Batuer Erkejin and Langtan to Kexitue with merit.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，從大將軍費揚古出西路，破敵昭莫多。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, when the Emperor campaigned in person against Galdan, he followed Grand General Fei Yanggu on the western route and broke the enemy at Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year (1696) he followed Fei Yanggu on the western route and fought at Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 以功授世職拖沙拉哈番，擢協領。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the hereditary rank of tosaha and promoted to assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: Merit brought a hereditary tosaha rank and promotion to assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，上幸西安閱武，設宴，特命額倫特近御座，親賜之飲。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, when the Emperor visited Xi'an to review troops, a banquet was set and E'lunte was specially ordered near the imperial seat and personally given drink.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year (1704), at the Xi'an review, he was seated near the Emperor and given wine.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「爾父宣力行間，爾亦入伍能效力，故賜爾飲。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Your father proclaimed merit on campaign; you too enlisted and could serve effectively, hence this drink is given you."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said his father had served well on campaign and he had done the same, and so honored him with wine.

sentences.zh: 尋遷西安副都統。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to deputy commander-in-chief of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) He soon became Xi'an deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 調荊州副都統。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commander-in-chief of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jingzhou deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，擢湖廣提督。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was promoted to provincial commander of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year (1710) he became Huguang provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was appointed governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year (1713) he became governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 尋命履勘湖南諸州縣荒壤，得四萬六千餘頃。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to survey wasteland in Hunan's prefectures and counties and found more than forty-six thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to survey Hunan wasteland and found more than forty-six thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 疏請聽民開墾，六年後以下則起科。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that people be allowed to open it; after six years the lower rate of tax would begin.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that settlers farm it with tax at the lower rate after six years.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，命往按太原知府趙鳳詔貪墨狀，論罪如律。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was ordered to investigate the corruption of Taiyuan prefect Zhao Fengshao; guilt was fixed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year (1715) he investigated Taiyuan Prefect Zhao Fengshao and punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 厄魯特策妄阿拉布坦犯哈密，上遣尚書富寧安等率師討之。

translations.literal: The Eleuth Tsewang Arabtan invaded Hami; the Emperor sent Minister Funinggan and others to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tsewang Arabtan invaded Hami the Emperor sent Funinggan and others against him.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，命額倫特署西安將軍，主軍餉。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year E'lunte was ordered to act as Xi'an general and manage army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year (1716) he acted as Xi'an general in charge of supplies.

sentences.zh: 策妄阿喇布坦自噶順汛山後道沙拉侵青海，執台吉羅卜藏丹濟布以去，命額倫特率師駐西寧，為青海諸部應援。

translations.literal: Tsewang Arabtan, by a route behind Gashun, crossed Shala to invade Qinghai and seized the taiji Lobzang Danjinbu; E'lunte was ordered to lead troops to garrison Xining as support for the Qinghai tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Tsewang Arabtan slipped behind Gashun through Shala into Qinghai and seized Lobzang Danjinbu; E'lunte garrisoned Xining to support the tribes.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，策妄阿拉布坦遣其將策淩敦多布侵西藏。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year Tsewang Arabtan sent his general Tsering Donduk to invade Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year (1717) Tsewang Arabtan sent Tsering Donduk into Tibet.

sentences.zh: 命額倫特移軍青海，與青海王台吉等議屯軍形勝地。

translations.literal: E'lunte was ordered to move his army to Qinghai and, with the Qinghai wang and taiji, discuss where to encamp troops on advantageous ground.
translations.idiomatic: E'lunte moved to Qinghai to choose camps with the Qinghai princes.

sentences.zh: 額倫特疏言西寧入藏道有三，庫庫賽爾嶺、拜都嶺道皆寬廣，請與侍衛色楞分道進兵。

translations.literal: E'lunte memorialized that three roads led from Xining into Tibet—the Kokosailin and Baidu routes were both broad and he asked to advance with Guardsman Seleng on separate roads.
translations.idiomatic: He reported three routes from Xining to Tibet, the Kokosailin and Baidu roads being widest, and asked to advance with Guardsman Seleng on separate columns.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，策淩敦多布入西藏，破布達拉城，戕拉藏汗，執其子蘇爾咱，遂據有其地。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year Tsering Donduk entered Tibet, broke Potala, killed the Dalai Lama Lozang Khan, seized his son Surten, and held the land.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year (1718) Tsering Donduk took Tibet, stormed Potala, killed Lozang Khan, seized his son Surten, and held the country.

sentences.zh: 六月，額倫特與色楞分道進兵，額倫特出庫庫賽爾嶺。

translations.literal: In the sixth month E'lunte and Seleng advanced on separate roads; E'lunte went out by Kokosailin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month E'lunte and Seleng marched separately; E'lunte took Kokosailin.

sentences.zh: 七月，至齊諾郭勒，策淩敦多布遣兵夜來侵，擊之退。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he reached Qinuogele; Tsering Donduk sent troops to attack by night and was beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month at Qinuogele the enemy attacked by night and was repulsed.

sentences.zh: 次日復至，額倫特親督兵緣山接戰，賊潰遁，追擊十餘裡，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: The next day they came again; E'lunte personally directed troops fighting along the mountain and the rebels fled; pursuit for more than ten li yielded many kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: They returned the next day; E'lunte fought along the heights, the rebels fled, and a ten-li pursuit brought heavy kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上深嘉其勇。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived the Emperor deeply praised his courage.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor deeply praised his courage when the report arrived.

sentences.zh: 俄，策淩敦多布遣兵潛出喀喇烏蘇，額倫特率所部疾趨渡河，扼狼拉嶺，據險禦敵。

translations.literal: Soon Tsering Donduk secretly sent troops out from Karusu; E'lunte led his command in haste to cross the river, seized Langla Ridge, and held difficult ground against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tsering Donduk slipped troops out from Karusu; E'lunte rushed to cross the river, held Langla Ridge, and blocked the pass.

sentences.zh: 比至喀喇烏蘇，色楞以兵來會，合力擊賊。

translations.literal: When they reached Karusu, Seleng came with troops to join and they struck the enemy together.
translations.idiomatic: At Karusu Seleng joined and they attacked together.

sentences.zh: 賊數万環攻，額倫特督兵與戰，被重創，戰益力。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of rebels surrounded them; E'lunte directed the fight and was badly wounded, yet fought all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands surrounded them; E'lunte was badly wounded yet fought harder.

sentences.zh: 相持者數月。

translations.literal: They held out for several months.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted months.

sentences.zh: 九月，复厲兵進戰，射殺賊甚眾。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again led troops forward; many rebels were shot down.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he attacked again and shot down many rebels.

sentences.zh: 矢盡，持刀麾兵斫賊，賊益兵合圍，額倫特中傷，猶力戰，遂沒於陣。

translations.literal: When arrows were exhausted he took a knife and waved troops to hack the enemy; the rebels added men and closed the ring. E'lunte was wounded again, still fought hard, and perished in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: When arrows ran out he drew a knife and led a charge; the enemy closed in. Wounded again, he fought on and fell in the line.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，喪還，上命諸王以下迎城外，內大臣、侍衛至其家奠茶酒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, when the coffin returned, the Emperor ordered princes and below to welcome it outside the city; interior ministers and guardsmen went to his home to offer tea and wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year (1719) princes welcomed his coffin outside the walls and ministers offered rites at his home.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，進世職三等阿達哈哈番，賜祭葬，諡忠勇。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne his hereditary rank was advanced to third-class adahahan, funeral honors were granted, and he was given the posthumous title Zhongyong.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng advanced his hereditary rank to third-class adahahan, granted funeral honors, and named him Zhongyong.

sentences.zh: 額倫特與川陝總督音泰皆自行伍中為上所識拔。

translations.literal: E'lunte and Shaanxi-Sichuan Governor-general Yintai were both men the Emperor had recognized and raised from the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: E'lunte and Governor-general Yintai of Shaanxi-Sichuan were both men the Emperor had raised from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 額倫特以廉潔著，上嘗與張伯行並稱，謂在督撫中操守最優也。

translations.literal: E'lunte was noted for integrity; the Emperor once named him together with Zhang Boxing, saying that among governors and governors-general his conduct was the finest.
translations.idiomatic: Known for integrity, he was once paired with Zhang Boxing as the cleanest of governors.

sentences.zh: 康泰，甘肅張掖人。

translations.literal: Kang Tai was a native of Zhangye, Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Tai was from Zhangye in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 初入伍，累擢至游擊。

translations.literal: At first he enlisted and was promoted step by step to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted and rose to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 從將軍孫思克擊噶爾丹，以功授世職拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: He followed General Sun Sike in attacking Galdan and, for merit, was granted the hereditary rank of tosaha.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Sun Sike against Galdan and received a hereditary tosaha rank.

sentences.zh: 四遷四川提督。

translations.literal: He was transferred four times to provincial commander of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He became Sichuan provincial commander after four promotions.

sentences.zh: 額倫特駐西寧，泰率松潘兵千餘出黃勝關為應援。

translations.literal: When E'lunte garrisoned Xining, Tai led more than a thousand Songpan troops out through Huang Shengguan as support.
translations.idiomatic: When E'lunte held Xining, Tai led more than a thousand Songpan troops through Huang Shengguan in support.

sentences.zh: 兵譟，奪官，命自具鞍馬從軍。

translations.literal: The troops mutinied; he was stripped of office and ordered to provide his own saddle horse and follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: His men mutinied; he lost his post and marched at his own expense.

sentences.zh: 從額倫特入藏，戰喀喇烏蘇，躍馬殺賊，矢集於臂，叱其子拔矢，裹臂复戰，陣沒。

translations.literal: He followed E'lunte into Tibet, fought at Karusu, leaped his horse to kill rebels, arrows clustered on his arm; he shouted for his son to pull them out, wrapped his arm, and fought again, and was killed in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: He followed E'lunte into Tibet, fought at Karusu, charged on horseback, took many arrows in the arm, had his son pull them, wrapped the wound, fought on, and fell in the line.

sentences.zh: 贈都督同知，諡壯勇。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Commissioner-in-chief and given the posthumous title Zhuangyong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Commissioner-in-chief with the name Zhuangyong.

sentences.zh: 弟海，陝西涼州總兵。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hai was regional commander of Liangzhou, Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hai was Liangzhou regional commander in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 將所部從額倫特，同時戰死。

translations.literal: He led his command to follow E'lunte and died in battle at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: He followed E'lunte with his command and died in the same fight.

sentences.zh: 贈世職拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the hereditary rank of tosaha.
translations.idiomatic: He received a posthumous hereditary tosaha rank.

sentences.zh: 論曰：厄魯特亦出於蒙古，析為四衛拉特，其一曰綽羅斯，牧伊犁。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Eleuths also came from the Mongols and split into the Four Oirats; one was the Choros, who pastured at Ili.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says the Eleuths were Mongols who split into the Four Oirats; the Choros pastured at Ili.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹戕兄子自立，乃號准噶爾，移帳阿爾泰山，兼有四衛拉特。

translations.literal: Galdan killed his brother's son and made himself ruler, then styled himself Dzungar, moved his camp to the Altai, and held all Four Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan killed his nephew, styled himself Dzungar, moved to the Altai, and ruled all Four Oirats.

sentences.zh: 北侵喀爾喀，南侵衛藏。

translations.literal: He invaded the Khalkha in the north and Tibet in the south.
translations.idiomatic: He raided the Khalkha northward and Tibet southward.

sentences.zh: 聖祖再親征，乃摧敗以死。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor campaigned in person twice and broke and destroyed him until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi campaigned twice in person and broke him until he died.

sentences.zh: 烏闌布通之役，噶爾丹敗遁，我軍亦重衄。

translations.literal: At Ulan Butung Galdan was beaten and fled, yet our army also suffered heavy losses.
translations.idiomatic: At Ulan Butung Galdan was beaten but our army suffered heavily too.

sentences.zh: 佟國綱以元舅死綏。

translations.literal: Tong Guogang died in harness as the Emperor's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guogang died in harness as the Emperor's uncle by marriage.

sentences.zh: 及戰昭莫多，費揚古麾飢疲之眾，當困鬥之寇，蹈瑕以破堅，則謀勇勝也。

translations.literal: When it came to fighting at Jao Modo, Fei Yanggu commanded hungry and weary troops against an enemy fighting desperately; striking at a weak point to break a solid line, strategy and courage prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: At Jao Modo, Fei Yanggu led hungry, exhausted men against a foe fighting for its life and broke a hard line by striking its weak point—strategy and courage won the day.

sentences.zh: 馬斯喀、阿南達、吉勒塔布、化行、育龍先後在事有勞。

translations.literal: Masika, A Nanda, Jileitabu, Huaxing, and Yulong each had merit in the affair in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Masika, A Nanda, Jileitabu, Yin Huaxing, and Pan Yulong each served with distinction in turn.

sentences.zh: 額倫特孤軍殉寇，青海之師，準部之滅，皆於是乎起。

translations.literal: E'lunte died with a lone army against the foe; the Qinghai campaign and the destruction of the Dzungar all arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: E'lunte fell with a lone army against the enemy; the Qinghai campaign and the fall of the Dzungars all began here.

sentences.zh: 謹書之以著其本末。

translations.literal: This is respectfully written to set forth the full course of events.
translations.idiomatic: This account is written to record the full story.
